# Triangle Restoration and Packing–Covering Stability in Tuza’s Conjecture

AI Math Experiments · 29 October 2026

## Abstract

For a finite simple graph $`G`$, let $`\nu(G)`$ be the maximum number of edge-disjoint triangles and $`\tau(G)`$ the minimum size of a triangle edge cover. We integrate triangle-restoration criteria and packing–covering stability results. Restoring one triangle to a remainder with tripartite full triangle hypergraph preserves Tuza’s inequality; consequently the inequality holds for odd-cycle transversal at most four and, by an adaptation of Liu–Zeng, for sufficiently large graphs with $`e(G)\ge n^2/4-cn`$ for every fixed $`c\lt 5/2`$. For two restored triangles we give complete proofs for exact-equality and essential-edge tripartite remainders, flat remainders, three specified nonflat star cores, and exact two-apex bowties with shared apices or mixed triangles. We prove closed-boundary deletion and stability criteria and a compression preserving four exact optimization values. Selected deductions are conditionally checked in Lean with their external mathematical inputs explicit; the remaining results have audited ordinary proofs. Unrestricted two-triangle restoration, OCT-five, and the fixed-$`c\lt 3`$ density extension remain unproved.

## 1. Introduction and contribution

Tuza’s conjecture asks whether $`\tau(G)\le2\nu(G)`$ for every finite simple graph $`G`$ \[[14](#reference-14)\]. The central mechanism here is a simultaneous compatibility argument: equality structure supplies a fixed old packing avoiding an entire family of newly restored triangles. Subsequent arguments study the rigidity left when this simple mechanism no longer applies.

## 2. Definitions and the one-triangle criterion

All graphs are finite, simple, and undirected. A triangle is a three-vertex clique, identified with its three edges when discussing packing and covering. For a triangle family $`\mathcal F`$, let $`\nu(\mathcal F)`$ be the maximum number of pairwise edge-disjoint members, and let $`\tau(\mathcal F)`$ be the minimum number of graph edges meeting every member. Both parameters are zero for the empty family. Write $`\nu(G),\tau(G)`$ for the full triangle family. The odd-cycle transversal number $`\mathrm{oct}(G)`$ is the minimum number of *vertices* whose deletion leaves a bipartite graph.

Each individual restoration must have actual cover increase three, since adding the other restored triangle’s three edges completes a cover of $`G`$. This uses actual tau of intermediate graphs, not just the cover number of a chosen new-family subcollection.

The adjacent-apex lemma is independently proved as follows. For any terminal $`u`$, deleting its pair of spokes preserves $`\tau(H)`$, because those two spokes and the opposite base cover the individual new family at cost three. If $`pq`$ were present, delete triangle $`upq`$. Aharoni and cover loss force equality with $`h-1`$ $`K_4`$ blocks. The terminal set $`\{u,p,q\}`$ is independent in the remainder, so choose one face avoiding it from each block, compatible with every lost triangle. The lost family has packing one, and contains $`pqa,pqb,pqc`$. A triangle not containing $`pq`$ cannot meet all three in edges: it would need three edges of the bipartite graph between $`\{p,q\}`$ and $`\{a,b,c\}`$, impossible. Thus all lost triangles contain $`pq`$, so $`pq`$ is essential. This contradicts stable $`H`$. Therefore same-family apex pairs are nonadjacent.

### 15.1 Exact formal boundary

The archived projects use Lean 4.33.1 and pinned Mathlib dependencies. All graph triangles are actual three-cliques and all extremal values are actual finite packing maxima and cover minima. HNSInput supplies edge-disjoint graphical $`K_4`$s and packages both published home-base extraction and the graphical loose-cycle conversion in Lemma [3.2](#lem-k4). Those inputs, including that conversion, remain assumed in Lean. Classical bipartite König matching–cover equality \[[11](#reference-11)\] is an explicit input to the boundary integrality theorem; the triangle-to-pair conversion, injectivity, matching compatibility and cover conversion are proved. Hall’s matching theorem \[[6](#reference-6)\] is used through the pinned formal library in the essential-edge proof.

### 15.3 Scope, originality and remaining questions

**Unrestricted two-triangle restoration, OCT-five and the fixed-$`c\lt 3`$ density extension remain unproved.** The density proof also establishes neither its endpoint $`c=5/2`$ nor a threshold uniform near that endpoint. General stable, nonflat, slack-one remainders remain outside the restoration theorems. Exact bowties with disjoint apices and no mixed triangle, and arbitrary individual families of packing three, are not settled here.

This paper follows those dependencies rather than the order of the TUZA-01, TUZA-02 and TUZA-03 investigations. The one-triangle criterion and its OCT and density consequences are retained with their complete proofs. The subsequent restoration and boundary deductions are integrated with their exact accepted hypotheses; selected supporting star-core results are included explicitly. Published inputs are attributed at their point of use. The verification boundary and open questions are collected in Section [15](#sec-verification).

The ordinary arguments use published mathematical theorems. Conditional Lean verification certifies specified deductions while retaining explicit Aharoni, graphical HNS and, where applicable, classical bipartite König inputs. In particular the inherited graphical HNS conversion is not independently discharged in Lean. Neither external specialist peer review nor established historical originality is claimed.

Tuza’s inequality for triangle-3-colorable graphs, including four-colorable graphs, is known from Lakshmanan–Bujtás–Tuza \[[3](#reference-3)\] and follows from Aharoni’s theorem \[[1](#reference-1)\]. The new deduction considered here is the addition of the three edges of a triangle to such a remainder. Merely adding these three edges to a cover loses one unit in the critical case. Equality structure repairs that loss. We use only the specific consequence of Haxell–Narins–Szabó (HNS) \[[9](#reference-9)\] proved below, rather than a classification of all graphical equality cases.

**Aharoni’s bound.** Every finite 3-partite 3-uniform hypergraph $`\mathcal H`$ satisfies $`\tau(\mathcal H)\le2\nu(\mathcal H)`$ \[[1](#reference-1)\]. An accessible formulation and derivation also appear in HNS, Section 3, Proposition 3.2(iii) and the following paragraph (author-manuscript p. 9). Thus $`\mathcal D(J)`$ 3-partite implies $`\tau(J)\le2\nu(J)`$.

**HNS’s equality characterization.** HNS Theorem 1.1 characterizes 3-partite 3-uniform hypergraphs with $`\tau=2\nu`$ as home-base hypergraphs \[[9](#reference-9)\]. We use the 18 March 2018 author manuscript: Definitions 7.1–7.4, pp. 19–20, and Proposition 7.5, p. 21. The earlier arXiv version has different numbering. HNS permits parallel hyperedges; simple hypergraphs are included.

For $`h=0`$, take the empty collection. Otherwise use the HNS partition. Choose a saturating matching in each $`B_i`$, and write $`w_i(R)`$ for the vertex matched to $`R`$. For each $`R`$ the hyperedges

form the required loose cycle. Its six vertices are distinct since $`W`$ is disjoint from the central triples and the three $`w_i(R)`$ lie in different parts. None belongs to any central triple or $`\mathcal A`$-piece. Thus these supports are disjoint simultaneously; no compatibility between the three matchings is missing. This is the extraction also used in the proof of HNS Proposition 7.5. Isolated vertices may remain in $`W`$.

After deleting $`E(T)`$ the only remaining edges inside $`S`$ join the possible fourth vertex to $`V(T)`$, so they form a subgraph of a star. Both $`H[S]`$ and $`H-S`$ are bipartite. Thus $`H`$ is four-colorable, and Lemma [4.2](#lem-colors) and Theorem [2.1](#thm-main) apply. The argument includes all smaller transversals and all configurations on $`S`$.

If it contained $`x`$ and touched two different e-pages through $`xw_1,xw_2`$, then $`yw_1w_2`$ would be a $`J`$-triangle sharing the block edge $`w_1w_2`$ but not a block face; exhaustion rules this out. When $`\nu(F)\le 2`$, Hall’s three-set criterion therefore fails only on all three sets: their total union has exactly two elements $`p,q`$. A graph apex occurs in one or three base sets, never exactly two. All sets are nonempty and no two are the same singleton, so both $`p`$ and $`q`$ occur in all three. $`F`$ consists exactly of $`T`$ plus its six pages on $`p,q`$.

Otherwise $`B,C`$ lie inside $`W`$ and are nonempty, not the same singleton. Their possible vertices are respectively $`\{z,r,t\}`$ and $`\{z,r,s\}`$. Independence and absence of neighbors $`a,c`$ force $`N_H(b) \cap W=\{r,s\}`$ or $`\{r,t\}`$; all other subsets make a set empty or make both the same singleton. By reflection take $`\{r,s\}`$. Then $`acz,abr,cbs,zst`$ are four edge-disjoint triangles: their edge sets are $`\{ac,az,cz\}`$, $`\{ab,ar,br\}`$, $`\{bc,cs,bs\}`$, $`\{zs,zt,st\}`$. This verifies the exceptional packing explicitly.

**Book core.** Suppose the residual component has $`\nu=\tau=1`$ and other components are $`K_4`$ copies. Choose block faces avoiding $`U`$. If $`\nu(F)\ge 3`$, append three $`F`$-triangles. Otherwise the essential-edge proof’s Hall classification gives apices $`p,q`$. Flatness forces $`pq`$ absent because otherwise $`pq`$ lies in the three old triangles $`pqu`$. Any old book triangle $`Q`$ therefore meets $`U`$ and $`\{p,q\}`$ each in at most one vertex, and has at most one page spoke. Two pages can avoid it as in the essential-edge proof, and append $`Q`$. In both cases packing increases by at least two over $`H`$.

**Restoration conclusion.** In slack one, if $`\nu(G)=h+2`$, each intermediate graph has packing $`h+1`$, so the augmentations force $`\tau(F_i)\le 2`$. Combine an old cover, one $`F_i`$-cover and the other restored triangle’s three edges. At slack at least two the old cover plus six edges suffices. At slack zero all triangles are isolated $`K_4`$ faces, and the exact-equality theorem’s elementary four-edge new-family cover argument applies. Hence the full theorem uses HKT and elementary arguments; neither Aharoni nor HNS is needed.

# Equality rigidity at degeneracy four and five

TUZA-04, 30 October 2026. Status: complete ordinary proofs, independently reconstructed by the root agent and the separate literature/adversarial-review agent. This is not external expert review and no Lean verification is claimed. Historical novelty is unestablished. The proof uses elementary finite graph arguments; no Aharoni or HNS input is needed for Theorems A and B. The restoration corollary separately uses the accepted one-triangle theorem of the frozen project manuscript.

## Statements

For a finite simple graph G, nu(G) is the maximum number of edge-disjoint triangles and tau(G) the minimum number of edges meeting every triangle. A triangle component is a component of the triangle-intersection graph in which two triangles are adjacent when they share an EDGE. A graph is d-degenerate if every nonempty subgraph has a vertex of degree at most d.

**Theorem A.** Every 4-degenerate graph G satisfies tau(G)<=2nu(G). Equality holds if and only if every nonempty triangle component consists exactly of the triangles of a K4 or K5. Additional triangle-free edges are permitted.

**Theorem B.** Every 5-degenerate graph G containing no K6-minus-one-edge as a SUBGRAPH satisfies tau(G)<=2nu(G). Equality holds if and only if every nonempty triangle component consists exactly of the triangles of a K4 or K5. The forbidden-subgraph condition is not merely an induced-subgraph condition. Additional triangle-free edges are permitted.

**Theorem B.** Every 5-degenerate graph G containing no K6-minus-one-edge as a SUBGRAPH satisfies tau(G)<=2nu(G). Equality holds if and only if every nonempty triangle component consists exactly of the triangles of a K4 or K5. The forbidden-subgraph condition is not merely an induced-subgraph condition. Additional triangle-free edges are permitted.

**Corollary B1.** For every K5-free 5-degenerate graph, Tuza holds and equality has exactly K4 triangle components. This follows because K6-minus-one-edge contains a K5.

**Corollary B1.** For every K5-free 5-degenerate graph, Tuza holds and equality has exactly K4 triangle components. This follows because K6-minus-one-edge contains a K5.

The inequality portions follow from known local reducibility arguments of Puleo. The proposed added contribution is equality rigidity with full triangle components, together with the explicit compatibility mechanism proving it. Corollary B1 contains the planar equality characterization of Cui--Haxell--Ma as a consequence, but the hypotheses here neither imply planarity nor require a global triangle-hypergraph tripartition.

## 1. Elementary block facts

K4 has (nu,tau)=(1,2). K5 has (nu,tau)=(2,4): two disjoint triangles exist; three disjoint triangles would use nine edges and leave one edge, impossible because every degree in a union of edge-disjoint triangles is even whereas removing one edge from K5 creates two odd degrees. Each edge of K5 meets three of its ten triangles, so three cover edges cannot cover them all; four edges inside a vertex bipartition of sizes two and three do cover all triangles.

## 2. Minimal-obstruction framework in a hereditary class

Call S the assertion that Tuza holds and equality has only K4/K5 triangle components. Let C be any class closed under taking subgraphs, and suppose G is a failure of S in C with as few edges as possible. Discard isolated vertices. Then every proper edge-subgraph satisfies S.

## 3. An edge cannot belong to just one triangle

Suppose uv belongs only to uvw. Delete uw,vw to get K. The edge uv is triangle-free in K, so every K-packing can be appended by uvw. A K-cover plus uw,vw covers G. Hence nu(K)=h-1, tau(K)=2h-2 and K has the block classification. Each block meets U0={u,v,w} at most once: uw,vw are absent, and uv is triangle-free in K.

## 4. Every link component has at least five vertices

Let C0 be a connected component of the link at v. In the following cases, deleting v means deleting just the spokes into C0; other neighbors of v remain. There is no triangle through a deleted spoke with its third vertex outside C0, because that would join link components. All listed covers therefore account for every lost triangle. External rim pages have apex outside C0 union {v}.

### 4.1 Link component K3

Write C0=abc. Delete its three v-spokes and ab. The triangle vab appends to any residual K-packing, and {ab,vc} is a cover increment, so K has equality blocks and nu(K)=h-1.

### 4.2 Link component K4

Write C0=abcd. Delete its v-spokes and ab,cd. The packing vab,vcd appends, and {ab,cd,va,vb} is a four-edge cover increment. Hence nu(K)=h-2 and K has equality blocks.

### 4.3 Diamond link component

Write C0=K4-ab on a,b,c,d. Delete its v-spokes and ac,bd. Use packing vac,vbd and cover increment {ac,bd,vc,vd}; equality gives nu(K)=h-2 and blocks.

### 4.4 Four-cycle link component

Let C0 be the cycle abcd. Delete its v-spokes and ab,cd,da, retaining bc. The packing vab,vcd appends; all four rim edges are a cover increment. Thus nu(K)=h-2, tau(K)=2h-4 and K has equality blocks.

## 5. A 3-colorable link component cannot have five vertices

Suppose a link component L has five vertices, minimum degree at least two, and is 3-colorable. Its complement has maximum degree at most two. A 3-coloring gives either a size-three color class (a triangle in the complement) or two size-two classes (a matching of size two). The possible complements are exactly

### 5.1 Four dense types

In each row |M|=|Q|=2. The listed three triangles are mutually edge-disjoint. Their edges present in the residual are in the next column. The missing and deleted edges restrict a block's intersection as shown, so maximum block packings avoid that set and append all three triangles, contradiction.

### 5.2 Three sparse types

For a bowtie L=abc union ade, take M={bc,de}, Q={a}. The cover increment has size three for a compatible two-packing, immediately strict.

### 5.3 The remaining type K221

Write the missing link edges ab,cd and the fifth link vertex e. The local graph B on W={v,a,b,c,d,e} is K6 minus ab,cd. Delete all B-edges to K. The four edge-disjoint triangles vac,vbd,ade,bce append to every K-packing. All eight rim edges cover every lost triangle through v and every other lost triangle. Hence equality forces nu(K)=h-4 and tau(K)=2h-8, and K has equality blocks. Each block meets W at most once, since W is independent in K.

### 5.4 One additional non-3-colorable link

The link consisting of K4 on a,b,c,d and a fifth vertex x adjacent exactly to a,b is also excluded. Take M={cd,ax} and Q={a,b}; L-Q is the single edge cd. Deleting the local v-spokes and M forces equality blocks with packing h-2. The triangles acd,vax,vbd are edge-disjoint and have old forbidden edges ac,ad,bd. A block cannot contain both ac,ad or both ac,bd because cd is deleted; the only possible pair is ad,bd, adjacent at d. Maximum block packings avoid this pair and append the three triangles, giving h+1, contradiction.

## 6. Deduction of Theorems A and B

For Theorem A, the class of 4-degenerate graphs is closed under subgraphs. A minimal failure of S in it would have minimum degree at least five by Section 4, contradicting degeneracy. Hence S holds. Conversely, disjoint triangle edge supports with K4/K5 components have additive nu,tau and equality, irrespective of triangle-free edges.

Corollary B1 follows because K5-free graphs cannot contain K6-minus-one-edge, and their equality components cannot be K5. Theorem A and Theorem B are incomparable: K6-minus-one-edge itself is 4-degenerate, so Theorem A is not redundant.

The same reasoning also proves the K4 equality classification for all 5-degenerate graphs whose vertex links are 3-colorable; this class is hereditary and excludes K5. This is subsumed by Corollary B1.

## 7. Restoration-specific corollary

Let R assert that if H has tripartite FULL triangle hypergraph and J=H+E(T), then equality tau(J)=2nu(J) forces K4/K5 triangle components. Suppose R fails; choose a failure minimizing old edge count. Any old-edge deletion stays in the one-triangle class, so the accepted one-triangle theorem supplies Tuza for every residual. If a nonempty such deletion leaves equality, minimality classifies its components.

**Corollary R-local.** After discarding isolated vertices, in an old-edge-minimal counterexample to R every vertex v outside U with at most one U-neighbor has all its link components of order at least six. In particular d_J(v)>=6.

This is a structural reduction toward restoration. It does not prove R or stable-remainder strictness. At a terminal, the analogous deletion can remove restored edges and is not authorized by this induction; the exact two-apex terminal link K2,3 plus a base edge is a concrete instance where that scope issue occurs.

## 8. Evidence and literature boundary

The proof was developed from the frozen TUZA manuscript at revision 97e913008e466de14f61437d8dae774946d92e8f, with external pages and K5 compatibility retained explicitly. The route's working history and superseded stopping points remain in EQUALITY_ROUTE.md.

## Audited deduction: when cover-preserving deletion destroys edge stability

**Statement.** Let D(H) be 3-partite, nu(H)=h, tau(H)=2h-1, and nu(H-g)=h for every graph edge g. Suppose tau(H-e)=tau(H), and H-e has a packing-essential edge f. Then the unique slack-one triangle component of H is exactly a central K4 with one or two leaf K4s attached on distinct spokes at a common central vertex, each leaf using two fresh vertices. All other triangle components are isolated K4 face families. Triangle-free background edges are permitted.

## Audited lifting observation

A tau-preserving edge deletion cannot first arrive at a five-wheel, K5 minus an edge, or a fresh one-/two-/three-leaf spoke-star defect (plus isolated equality blocks). Reason: every newly recovered triangle Q must meet the stable defect R in at least two old edges; otherwise maximum packings in R and each isolated block can avoid Q and Q augments. Thus Q lies within R. Every missing internal edge in a spoke-star closes a hub triangle disjoint from the packing of opposite base faces; every missing rim chord in W5 produces a three-packing; completing K5 minus an edge raises tau from 3 to 4. Each contradicts preservation of nu or tau. This is also a reconstruction of an existing private draft, not a new claim of novelty.

## Exact two-apex cover switching

Assume the precise Corollary 11.3 configuration: independent U={a,b,c}, independent P={p,q}, exactly the seven new triangles abc and six universal-apex pages, stable H with (nu,tau)=(h,2h-1), restored J with (nu,tau)=(h+1,2h+2).

## Obstacles and routes not to repeat

- The four-spoke descent changes the new family; it cannot be iterated as if the original seven-triangle family survived.
- Existing availability formula maximizes over ALL packings of H minus the six spokes. Restricting to maximum packings may miss a smaller packing with more available rows.
- A nonmonochromatic apex recoloring exchanges into the unresolved new-family packing-three branch; it is not a solution of that branch.
- Kempe locking statements are conditional on eliminating that packing-three branch and concern different deleted graphs; their component partitions cannot be unioned.
- Cover-excluded edges need not be triangle-free or absent in stable slack-one graphs. The two-K4 shared-edge core provides active excluded edges.
- No proof here rules out an invisible K2,3 whose two parts are independent, or the exact two-apex cover-switching configuration.

## Stronger new deduction: all six spokes are active

This was developed during TUZA-04 from the accepted Corollary 11.3 and the elementary zero-cost row deletion, independently checked by this route. It improves the qualified five-active-spoke premise to all six in the precise critical configuration.

**Theorem.** Under the exact Corollary 11.3 hypotheses (stable tripartite slack-one H; independent terminal triple; exactly two nonadjacent universal apices; actual restored parameters nu(J)=h+1 and tau(J)=2h+2), every one of the six spokes belongs to an old H-triangle.

Deleting all six spokes S does not give tau(H-S)>=tau(J)-6 merely because S covers all pages: S misses the restored triangle abc. The unconditional cover bound uses S plus one restored base, hence seven edges, leaving nu(H-S) in {h-2,h-1}. A six-edge bound is available if an inactive spoke can be omitted and a base added, but the theorem above now rules out such inactive spokes in the critical stable configuration. Do not reuse the invalid generic six-edge bound.

## Further consequence: defective packing number at least five

For a terminal u, let L_u be all old triangles using up or uq. Exactness makes L_u a bipartite matching family between {p,q} and the outside neighbors of u. Different rows have disjoint edge supports. All six spokes are active by the new theorem, so each row matching number is either one or two.

## Exact cover-profile interface for the restored graph

Let S be the six spokes, K=H-S, and F the seven-triangle bipyramid family. For **any** edge cover C of all K-triangles with C subset E(K), define R(C) subset S by putting ur in R(C) exactly when some old H-triangle on ur is not met by C. These are required spokes if the rest of the cover is chosen within S. The optimization ranges over ALL K-covers, not merely minimum or inclusion-minimal ones; triangle-free K-edges may help cover lost triangles and cannot be discarded in advance.

Suppose nu(K)=h-2 and write k=h-2. Then tau(K)=2k-1 and K is stable, as proved above. Let R_u be a complete terminal row of two S-spokes. For any distinct rows u,v, K+R_u+R_v is H with the third row deleted, hence has tau=t=tau(K)+4. Consequently, for EVERY subset A of those four spokes,

## 1. Exact statement and hypotheses

Let C be any class closed under subgraphs, and let G be an edge-minimal failure in C of S: Tuza's inequality together with equality classification into K4/K5 triangle components. Delete isolated vertices. Use the audited TUZA-04 premises: G has connected triangle support, tau(G)=2nu(G), all proper edge-subgraphs satisfy S, every edge has triangle codegree at least two, every link component has order at least five, and every degree-five vertex has link K5 or K5 minus one edge.

**Proposition P7.** If v has degree five and u is a neighbor dominating its link (equivalently N[v] is contained in N[u]), then d(u)>=8.

For a clique link every neighbor dominates. For a link K5-ab, the three neighbors other than a,b dominate.

**Corollary.** Every 5-degenerate graph of maximum degree at most seven satisfies S. Proof: this is a hereditary class; a minimal failure has minimum degree at least five and thus a degree-five vertex. Its link has one of the two forms above, hence a dominating neighbor; P7 contradicts maximum degree seven.

The corollary allows K6 and K6-minus-edge subgraphs, so is not contained in frozen TUZA-04 Theorem B. Its inequality is already covered by Gupta's maximum-degree-seven theorem; the proposed advance is equality classification under the additional 5-degeneracy hypothesis. No claim of historical priority is made.

## 2. Packing and cover accounting

Write W=N(v)-{u}, B=G[{u,v} union W], Z=N(u)-N[v], and k=|Z|=d(u)-5. As u dominates v, W has four vertices, B is K6 or K6-ab, and every neighbor of u lies in {v} union W union Z. The vertex v has no neighbor in Z. Edges from W or Z to vertices outside this set remain unrestricted.

## 3. Dominating neighbors of degree at most six

Take X=E(G[W]) union {uv} union {uz:z in Z}. It meets all triangles incident to u or v.

## 4. B=K6-ab and d(u)=7

Here Z has two vertices. Take X=E(W) union {uv} union uZ, of size eight, and any four-packing of B. Equality forces K=G-u-v-E(W) to have residual blocks.

## 5. B=K6 and d(u)=7

Write Z={p,q}. There are two cases.

### 5.1 pq is present

Take P to be a four-packing of B plus upq. Set
X=E(W) union {uv,up,uq,pq}.
Its size is ten. It covers every triangle incident to u or v, and contains every P-edge not incident to them, so K=G-u-v-E(W)-pq has equality blocks.

### 5.2 pq is absent

The codegree bound on up and uq implies that p and q each have at least two neighbors in W.

## 6. Additional adjacent degree-five restriction

This is not required for the corollary but is a separate equality upgrade of Puleo's common-neighborhood-three case.

## 7. Relation to published reductions and limits

The pair-reduction framework and balanced common-neighborhood-three template are from Puleo, arXiv:1308.2211v3, Proposition 5.2; the subsumed degree-seven/eight analysis is Lemma 7.5. Those published statements concern reducibility for an inequality counterexample. A minimal S failure need not have no balanced reducible set. ## 8. Degree-eight upgrade: Proposition P8

**Proposition P8.** Under the same minimal-obstruction hypotheses, every dominating neighbor u of a degree-five vertex v has degree at least nine.

**Proposition P8.** Under the same minimal-obstruction hypotheses, every dominating neighbor u of a degree-five vertex v has degree at least nine.

### 8.1 Z is independent, either core

Every z in Z has at least two neighbors in W by the codegree-at-least-two property of uz. Let J be the bipartite graph between Z and W.

### 8.2 Z contains an edge pq and B=K6-ab

Use a four-packing of B together with upq, and set
X=E(W) union {uv} union uZ union {pq}.
This is a balanced five/ten reduction. The residual has W independent and pq absent.

### 8.3 Z contains an edge pq and B=K6

Let Z* be the vertices of Z having at least one W neighbor.

**Corollary P8.** Every 5-degenerate graph of maximum degree at most eight satisfies S. Suppose v has degree five, its link is K5-ut, and u is one of the two nondominating positions. Thus N(v)={u,t,a,b,c}, with ut absent. Suppose d(u)=6. Its remaining two neighbors are p,q, both outside N[v], and W={a,b,c} is the common neighborhood. In G-u, the vertices {v,t,a,b,c} induce K5.

## 10. Overlap restriction for nonadjacent degree-five vertices

**Proposition O.** Two nonadjacent degree-five vertices x,y have at most three common neighbors. If they have exactly three, both links must be K5.

**Proposition O.** Two nonadjacent degree-five vertices x,y have at most three common neighbors. If they have exactly three, both links must be K5.

### 10.2 Four common neighbors

Write W=C and let p,q be the respective unique neighbors outside the common neighborhood. The graph on W is K4 or K4 minus one edge. It has two edge-disjoint perfect matchings, so four triangles, two at each center, form a packing.

If a common edge ac is absent, write C={a,b,c}, N(x)-C={p,q}, N(y)-C={r,s}. Both links are precisely K5-ac; all edges required below therefore exist. The pairs p,q and r,s are disjoint, because C is exactly the common neighborhood.

### 10.4 Three common neighbors, a missing edge outside C

Suppose C is a triangle and at least one link is K5 minus an edge; take that link to be the one at y. Let its missing edge be e. At least one endpoint of e lies outside C. Choose an edge f=ac of C disjoint from e and let b be the third vertex.

## 11. The global peeling reduction and final local configuration

This section records a proposed closure of the full 5-degenerate target. Every preceding local result must be independently checked before this conclusion is accepted.

### 11.1 The four cross edges are forced

Suppose one of the four edges joining {b,c} to {d,e} is absent. Relabel within each pair so that ce is absent.

### 11.2 The final eight-vertex graph B

Let B be the graph induced on {u,v,w,a,b,c,d,e}. It has A=K5, u joined to all other seven vertices, v joined within B precisely to u,a,b,c, and w joined within B precisely to u,a,d,e. The only further neighbors of v,w in G are p,q respectively.

### 11.3 External-page augmentation closes the configuration

Delete u,v,w and every A-edge, obtaining K. The seven-packing of B appends to every K-packing. The fourteen edges
X=E(A) union {uv,uw,vp,wq}
cover every triangle lost in the deletion. Triangles at u are inside B; triangles at v or w are inside B or use vp or wq; other lost triangles use an A-edge. Equality therefore forces
nu(K)=nu(G)-7, tau(K)=2nu(K),
and K has K4/K5 triangle components. Since A is independent in K, each block meets A at most once.

## 12. Proposed resulting theorem and review boundary

**Theorem candidate.** Every finite simple 5-degenerate graph G satisfies tau(G)<=2nu(G). Equality holds if and only if every nonempty triangle component is the full triangle family of a K4 or K5. Triangle-free background edges are allowed.

**Theorem candidate.** Every finite simple 5-degenerate graph G satisfies tau(G)<=2nu(G). Equality holds if and only if every nonempty triangle component is the full triangle family of a K4 or K5. Triangle-free background edges are allowed.

### Seven-edge rim lemma

Every graph L with seven edges on five vertices contains a triangle C and two edge-disjoint hub triangles whose rim bases avoid E(C). Indeed, L contains a triangle by the five-vertex Mantel bound. The four edges of L-E(C) either contain a matching of size two, which gives the hub triangles, or form a four-star: an intersecting graph-edge family with at least four edges is a star. In the latter case write C=abc, star center s, and fourth leaf d. The center s is outside C, since every triangle vertex has two of its incident edges deleted. Use sab as the new rim triangle and the disjoint remaining edges sd and ac as hub bases. The three triangles are sab,vsd,vac.

Again the residual triangle components would be equality blocks. If F is nonempty, take one page on base f and a four-packing of B-f. Every residual block can avoid its at-most-one old page spoke, so these five triangles append to a K packing, giving h+1. If F is empty, a six-edge B cover gives tau(G)<=2k+6<2h. Thus sigma(K) is 1 or 2.

If two external pages are edge-disjoint, their distinct bases can be deleted and the seven-edge rim lemma supplies three local triangles. Each residual equality block avoids at most two old spokes, so the five triangles append to a K packing, giving h+1. Hence F would be pairwise intersecting. Assume now sigma(K)=1 and an edge e=pq is packing-essential. Put Q=K-e and q=nu(Q)=k-1. Since a single edge deletion lowers the cover number by at most one,

### One touched spoke per equality block, and existence of a free page

Every triangle of K absent from Q is an e-page pqt. A Q clique block cannot contain both p and q. If it contained two old spokes pt1,pt2 from e-pages, it would contain t1t2. But qt1t2 is then a Q triangle sharing the block edge t1t2, forcing q into the same triangle component and hence the same clique block. This would force the absent edge pq, a contradiction. The same applies with p,q exchanged. Thus each block contains at most one old spoke across the entire e-page family.

Suppose an external page P is edge-disjoint from A. A four-packing of B minus P's base, together with A and P, extends a maximum Q packing: each Q block needs to avoid only its at-most-one P spoke, and A's old edges are outside all blocks. This gives q+6=h+1, contradiction.

Together with A,P1,P2 these extend a maximum Q packing to q+6=h+1. The only block avoidance requirements come from the at-most-two old page spokes, since A is free. This is impossible, so F0 is pairwise intersecting.

The surviving K6-ab remainder is a packing-edge-stable graph with integer deficit one. The surviving K6 remainder either has the same stability and deficit one, or has deficit two. The elementary obstruction to an unjustified extension is that a maximum K5 packing cannot avoid a three-edge star. The free-page argument above legitimately avoids that obstruction only after deleting an essential edge from a deficit-one remainder.

# Cover-preserving loss of packing stability with K4/K5 equality blocks

Status: complete ordinary conditional structural lemma, proposed for use inside a minimum-S-counterexample proof. This extends the frozen tripartite boundary deduction to equality remainders with K5 blocks and replaces its adjacent-edge appeal to a tripartite closed-boundary theorem by a direct argument. It does not classify arbitrary stable deficit-one graphs. No computation or Lean check was run. Historical novelty is unassessed; the K4-only source is frozen TUZA-04 BOUNDARY_ROUTE.md.

## Exact statement

Let K have nu(K)=k, tau(K)=2k-1, with nu(K-f)=k for every edge f. Let d be an edge with tau(K-d)=tau(K), and suppose K-d has a packing-essential edge e. Put Q=K-{d,e}. Assume Q satisfies Tuza and, at equality, has only K4/K5 triangle components. These assumptions are supplied when K is a proper edge-subgraph of a minimum failure of combined statement S in a hereditary class.

## Forced equality and the free e-page

Stability gives nu(K-d)=k, and essentiality gives nu(Q)=k-1=q. As tau(K-d)=2k-1, one-edge cover loss and Tuza imply tau(Q)=2q. Thus the triangle components of Q are K4/K5 blocks.

## Adjacent d,e are impossible

Rename adjacent edges d=px and e=py. A free e-page has form A=pyr with r different from x, because d is absent in K-d. Any d-page in K-e that meets A must be B=pxr.

## Disjoint d,e force the central K4

Return to e=xy and the free A=xyz. A d-page intersecting A, with d disjoint from xy, forces d=zw for a fourth vertex w, and its apex is x or y. Choose B=xzw, interchanging x,y if necessary.

## Attachment structure and deficit

The central K4 can meet old block supports only on xw and yw: xy,zw are absent from Q, and xz,yz are free. The two possible attachment edges belong to different blocks, since a block containing both would contain the absent xy. A block attached on xw cannot also contain y or z, because this would require xy or zw; similarly for yw. Two attached blocks cannot share an additional vertex t, since both would then contain wt and belong to the same triangle component. Their private vertices are therefore distinct, as claimed.

## Use and limitation

In a dense-link deficit-one remainder, this identifies the only possible structural result of a cover-preserving deletion that first destroys packing-edge stability, provided the equality descendant remains within the minimum-counterexample induction. It does not show such a deletion sequence exists, preserve tau under unions of deletions, or show an arbitrary stable remainder has this form. Any proposed iteration must prove its own total cover preservation.

## Corollary for the localized K6 deficit-one remainder

The exceptional component in the lemma has independence number at most three: at most one vertex can be chosen in the central clique, and at most one private vertex from each of at most two leaf cliques. Consequently, for the localized K6 deficit-one remainder described in DENSE_REMAINDER_AUDIT.md, any tau-preserving single-edge deletion preserves packing-edge stability. Otherwise the lemma would classify its unique deficit-one component as one of these cores, whereas it contains the five independent rim vertices.

# Equality in Tuza's Inequality for 5-Degenerate Graphs

**AI-developed mathematical research report — AI Math Experiments**  
Technical report · Editorial revision, 30 October 2026

## Abstract

We characterize equality in Tuza's triangle packing–covering inequality for finite simple 5-degenerate graphs. Equality holds exactly when every nonempty triangle component, connected through shared graph edges, has edge support $K_4$ or $K_5$. We prove the combined statement, including $\tau(G)\le2\nu(G)$, where $\nu(G)$ is the maximum number of edge-disjoint triangles and $\tau(G)$ is the minimum number of graph edges meeting every triangle. Triangle-free background edges and clique blocks sharing vertices are allowed; graph order and maximum degree are unrestricted. The inequality has a short deduction from published local reductions. The equality classification requires additional residual-packing compatibility and a strict-cover saving for arbitrary outside attachments. The exact combined theorem has been checked in Lean with pinned dependencies. Historical priority and external specialist peer review remain unestablished.

## Introduction and precise contribution

The equality classification is the principal contribution proposed in this report. Tuza's conjecture [1] asks whether $\tau(G)\le2\nu(G)$ holds for every finite simple graph. We establish the inequality together with its exact equality characterization in the subgraph-closed class of 5-degenerate graphs. ## 4. Every link component has at least five vertices

**Lemma 5 (Robustness).** Every connected component of every vertex link in a minimal combined obstruction has at least five vertices; in particular the obstruction $G$ has minimum degree at least five.

## 5. Complete classification of five-vertex links

**Lemma 6 (Degree-five links).** The link of every degree-five vertex in a minimal combined obstruction is $K_5$ or $K_5$ minus one edge.

The missing and deleted edges restrict a block's intersection as shown, so every whole block footprint is a star with at most two edges. Lemma 2A appends all three triangles, contradiction.

### 5.2 Three sparse types

### 5.3 The remaining type $K_{2,2,1}$

### 5.4 One additional non-3-colorable link

### 5.5 The two remaining degree-five links

Every $K_4$-free graph on at most five vertices is 3-colorable. Indeed, a vertex-minimal graph that is not 3-colorable has minimum degree at least 3. On four vertices it is $K_4$; on five its complement is a matching. $K_5$ minus zero or one edge contains $K_4$, while $K_5$ minus two independent edges is $K_{2,2,1}$ and is 3-colorable.

## 6. Degree-five vertices are independent and have no degree-six neighbor

**Lemma 7 (Low-neighbor restriction).** Degree-five vertices form an independent set in a minimal combined obstruction, and every neighbor of such a vertex has degree at least seven.

*Proof.*

### 6.1 Dominating neighbors of degree five or six

Let $v$ have degree 5 and let $u$ be a neighbor with $N[v]\subseteq N[u]$. Write $W=N(v)-\{u\}$, $B=G[\{u,v\}\cup W]$, and $Z=N(u)-N[v]$. Then $B$ is $K_6$ or $K_6$ minus one rim edge, and $|Z|=d(u)-5$.

### 6.2 Adjacent degree-five vertices

Otherwise, their precise links force three common neighbors $W=\{w_1,w_2,w_3\}$. Both links are $K_5$ minus one edge. Let $p$ be the unique neighbor of $u$ outside $N[v]$ and $q$ the unique neighbor of $v$ outside $N[u]$. The vertices $p$,$q$ are distinct, each joins all of $W$, $vp$ and $uq$ are absent, and $W$ is a triangle. Whether $pq$ is present is irrelevant.

### 6.3 A nondominating degree-six neighbor

## 9. Conclusion, converse and scope

The class of finite 5-degenerate graphs is closed under every vertex and edge deletion used above. If it contained a failure of $S$, choose one with the fewest edges and discard isolates. Sections 1–5 give the minimal-obstruction premises. Sections 6–8 exclude it. Hence every graph in this class satisfies the inequality and the asserted necessity at equality.

The equality classification is the principal contribution proposed in this report. Tuza's conjecture [1] asks whether $\tau(G)\le2\nu(G)$ holds for every finite simple graph. We establish the inequality together with its exact equality characterization in the subgraph-closed class of 5-degenerate graphs. **Equivalent block formulation.** The component condition is equivalent to the existence of a finite family of pairwise edge-disjoint actual $K_4$ and $K_5$ subgraphs containing every graph triangle. To prove this, component supports give such a family directly. Conversely, assign each triangle to a containing block. Triangles in different blocks cannot share an edge, by edge disjointness. Within $K_4$ or $K_5$ its triangles are connected by shared edges: two triangles sharing only a vertex are joined by a triangle using that vertex and one other vertex from each. Every block edge belongs to a triangle. Thus a triangle component consists exactly of one block's full triangle family, and its literal edge support is that clique. This argument checks the literal component condition rather than assuming it from a supplied decomposition. Since packing and covering numbers add over edge-disjoint triangle supports, the elementary parameters in Lemma 2 prove the equality converse for arbitrary graphs.

The proof's starting framework is due to Puleo [2, Definition 2.1 and Lemma 2.2]. Cui, Haxell and Ma [4, Theorem 1.2 and Section 2] characterize planar equality using edge-disjoint $K_4$ copies containing every triangle, with triangle-free background edges allowed. Theorem 1 recovers their known case because planar graphs are 5-degenerate and contain no $K_5$. Their theorem is not claimed as a new consequence in historical terms. Puleo's main sparsity theorem assumes maximum average degree less than seven. This class and the class of all five-degenerate graphs are incomparable. The graph $K_7$ has maximum average degree six but is not five-degenerate. # Further Investigations of Tuza's Conjecture: Equality Extensions, Cover Switching, and Integrality Obstructions

**AI-developed mathematical research report — AI Math Experiments**

## Abstract

This technical companion consolidates TUZA-07–10. Over graphs whose triangle components have literal $K_4$ or $K_5$ support, a constructive packing-or-cover completion yields a gain-one inequality and an exact two-alternative equality classification. Conditional minimal-counterexample deductions describe deletion resilience and extension of every prescribed packing of one or two triangles. An arbitrary-graph cover-switch theorem has explicit equal-cover and exactly-two-common-neighbor hypotheses; its sharp obstruction is a non-tight seven-vertex graph. B1/B2, the conditional A1 deductions and the universal cover-switch theorem have symbolic Lean proofs; W7 sharpness has ordinary and finite verification. Subsequent ordinary arguments and exact certificates refute unrestricted multicover splitting, half-cost rounding and an abstract colored-system half-integrality reduction. A restricted cycle theorem follows from known color-line and Brooks methods. General Tuza, the colored question R and the proposed general $5/3$ refinement remain unproved. No credible general proof bridge or historical originality is established.

## 1. Scope, definitions and previous work

For a finite simple graph $G$, let $\mathcal T(G)$ be its **full** family of triangles, $\nu(G)$ its maximum number of pairwise edge-disjoint triangles, and $\tau(G)$ the minimum number of actual graph edges meeting every triangle. Tuza's conjecture [@Tuza1990] asks whether $\tau(G)\le2\nu(G)$ for every such graph. It remains OPEN in this report. A notation such as $uv$ denotes the unordered graph edge, while $uvw$ denotes the triangle on three distinct vertices. Deleting edges retains the vertex set. An old-support edge lies in an old triangle, rather than merely being an old graph edge.

## 2. Block-type completion and gain-one equality

The mathematical headlines are B1 (constructive completion and scalar consequences) and B2 (full gain-one equality and converse). Historical notes used the label "B2" once for a four-edge corollary; this report consistently reserves B2 for equality rigidity. The three/four-edge statements are consequences.

### Exact hypotheses

H and G are finite simple graphs on a common vertex set, with E(H) subset E(G). Adding isolated vertices to H permits arbitrary new vertices. Every nonempty triangle component of H, where triangles are joined through shared graph edges, has literal edge support a complete K4 or K5. All H edges not in these supports are allowed; they lie in no H triangle. Let h=nu(H), and let N be the family of G triangles that are not H triangles. Thus tau(H)=2h. No degeneracy or degree assumption is made on G or its triangle-free background.

#### Theorem B1 (packing-gain-one cover completion)

If nu(G)=h+1, then tau(G)<=2h+2.

#### Four-addition corollary

If |E(G) minus E(H)|<=4, then tau(G)<=2nu(G).

### Local facts and proofs

1. Each new triangle Q uses at most one old edge in any one H block. Indeed two edges of a triangle share a vertex and contain all its vertices. If two belong to one clique block, its third edge also belongs to that block and hence H, contradicting Q being new.

### Compatible pair principle

Two new triangles P,Q can be appended simultaneously to some maximum H packing provided (a) they are edge-disjoint and (b) there is no K4 block in which their respective old edges form an opposite pair. Each uses at most one edge per old block by Fact 1. In a K5 block the two old edges can be avoided by Fact 3; in K4 the allowed pair can be avoided by Fact 2. Taking a maximum packing in each block avoiding their old edges then appending P,Q proves nu(G)>=h+2.

### Proof of B1

First, any individual new triangle can be appended to a maximum H packing because it uses at most one old edge per block. Hence any nonempty N raises nu by at least one.

### Elementary pairwise-intersecting triangle-family lemma

Let F be any nonempty family of graph triangles with no edge-disjoint pair. If all triangles share one edge, that edge covers F. Otherwise choose two distinct triangles abc and abd, c!=d, sharing ab. Some R avoids ab and intersects both. Its meeting edges cannot be disjoint, so R is acd or bcd; exchange a,b to take R=acd. Any triangle meeting all three abc,abd,acd must lie on {a,b,c,d}: a triangle using an outside vertex cannot contain two different edges of the displayed triangle family, since any two such incident edges already contain three of a,b,c,d; a single such edge common to all three does not exist. Hence F is contained in the four faces of this K4. Any opposite edge pair covers it. Thus an edge cover of size at most two exists.

### Proof of the four-addition corollary

If N is empty, both optima equal those of H and Tuza holds. Otherwise q=nu(G)-h>=1. If q=1, apply B1. If q>=2, any minimum H cover together with all at most four added edges covers G, so tau(G)<=2h+4<=2(h+q)=2nu(G). No assertion about general Tuza is used.

### Constructive packing/cover dichotomy

Let H have only literal K4/K5 triangle components, G be any supergraph, and h=nu(H). There is a finite constructive procedure returning either (a) a G triangle packing of size h+2, or (b) a G triangle cover of size at most 2h+2.

### Exact statement (A9 / B1 equality strengthening)

Let H be a finite simple graph whose nonempty shared-edge triangle components have literal K4 or K5 edge supports. Let G be any finite simple supergraph on the same vertex set (new vertices may first be adjoined to H as isolates). Write h=nu(H), so tau(H)=2h. Suppose
nu(G)=h+1 and tau(G)=2h+2.

### Inputs from B1

The proven gain-one cover-completion argument in [GAIN_ONE_THEOREM.md](../../problems/TUZA-07/notes/GAIN_ONE_THEOREM.md) supplies:

### Case I: N is pairwise edge-intersecting

If every N triangle shares one edge, adjoining that edge to a minimum H cover gives tau(G)<=2h+1, contradiction.

### Case II: N contains an edge-disjoint pair P,Q

The input above forces an old K4 B with vertices a,b,c,d and
P=abx, Q=cdy,
where ab,cd are opposite B edges, and x,y lie outside B. The only old support edge in P is ab, and in Q it is cd.

#### Different apices x!=y are impossible at equality

P and Q then have disjoint vertex sets.

#### Equal apices x=y=z force exactly one K5

P=abz and Q=cdz show that z is adjacent in G to every B vertex. Because B is a K4, ALL six z-pages on B edges therefore occur in N.

### Corollary: three-edge combined preservation

If G is obtained from block-type H by adding at most THREE edges, then Tuza holds and equality occurs only with K4/K5 triangle components.

## 3. Conditional edge-minimal-counterexample deductions

All statements in this section assume an actual edge-minimal violation. No such graph is asserted to exist. The component-connectedness observation below is an ordinary deduction; it was not included among the formal A1 targets. The one/two-triangle and wedge statements were formalized with addition equations to avoid natural-number subtraction ambiguity.

### Definitions and hypothesis

G is a finite simple graph that violates Tuza and is edge-minimal among actual violations: tau(G)>2nu(G), and every proper edge-subgraph satisfies Tuza. Isolated vertices are irrelevant. Set k=nu(G). This is different from an edge-minimal failure of Tuza plus the K4/K5 equality classification.

### A1. One-edge criticality — PROVED

For every edge e:
nu(G-e)=k, tau(G-e)=2k, tau(G)=2k+1.

### A2. General edge-deletion resilience — PROVED

For every nonempty S subset E(G),
nu(G)-nu(G-S) <= floor((|S|-1)/2).

### A3. Every one- or two-triangle packing extends — PROVED

Let P be p pairwise edge-disjoint G triangles with p=1 or p=2. Then
nu(G-E(P))=k-p.
Consequently P is contained in some maximum packing of G.

### A5. Minimum triangle codegree two — PROVED, known predecessor

Suppose uv belongs to only triangle uvw. Delete uw and vw to obtain K. The edge uv is triangle-free in K, so every K packing appends uvw; hence nu(K)<=k-1. But A2 says deleting two edges preserves k, contradiction.

### Limitations

The hypotheses involve an actual minimal counterexample. No such graph is known. These identities expose necessary obstruction structure; they do not show it is impossible. Claiming that the residual tight graphs have K4/K5 support would import the unrestricted equality conjecture.

## 5. Multicover and fractional-integrality obstructions

No new Lean theorem is claimed in TUZA-09. The following elementary proofs and exact graphs identify failed mechanisms. They are not counterexamples to Tuza. The CKSU trace is a source-specific inference, distinguished from a full algorithm implementation replay.

### A. Exact splitting criterion

Let `m:E(G)->{0,1,2}` be any 2-fold multicover. Set `D={e:m(e)=2}` and `S={e:m(e)=1}`. For every triangle avoiding D, either two or three edges belong to S. Define constraints on colors of S:

**Proposition A (PROVED_ORDINARY).** The multiset m can be partitioned into two ordinary triangle covers if and only if these pair and triple constraints admit a two-coloring.

**Proof.** If a partition exists and both copies of a double edge occur on one side, move one copy to the other side. The donor still contains that edge, so its coverage is unchanged; the recipient cannot lose coverage. Normalize all double edges this way. Each side now contains D. Every remaining triangle must see a singleton copy on both sides, giving precisely the constraints. Conversely, place one copy of D on each side and partition S by a satisfying coloring. A triangle containing D is hit on both sides. Every other triangle is hit on both sides by the applicable pair or triple condition. Each side is an ordinary set. QED.

### B. An optimal, budget-tight K5 multicover that cannot split

Take vertices 1,2,3,4,5. Put multiplicity 0 on 12 and 34, and multiplicity 1 on all other edges. Its total is 8. No triangle contains both zero edges, so every triangle has load at least 2.

### C. K6: a nonsplittable optimal multicover in the CKSU construction

Let G=K6 on vertices 1,...,6, and put m=0 on the perfect matching `{12,34,56}`, m=1 elsewhere. Each triangle contains at most one matching edge, so m is a 2-cover of total 12.

### D. Even optimal 2-cover cost cannot universally be halved

Let F be triangle-free and form G by adding an apex a adjacent to every vertex of F. Its only triangles are `{a,u,v}` for `uv in E(F)`.

**Proposition D (PROVED_ORDINARY, known reduction context).** $\nu(G)=m(F)$ and $\tau(G)=\operatorname{vc}(F)$, where $m$ is the ordinary matching number.

**Proof.** Two apex triangles share an edge exactly when their base edges share an endpoint. Thus edge-disjoint triangles correspond exactly to matchings. A vertex cover U of F gives the triangle cover `{au:u in U}`. Conversely, from any triangle cover C, replace every selected base edge uv by one endpoint spoke au, keeping existing spokes and dropping duplicates. The removed base edge occurs in only its own apex triangle, and its replacement hits that triangle, so this operation cannot uncover any triangle. The final selected spokes correspond to a vertex cover of F and are no more numerous than C. QED.

## 6. Colored supports, forced one-third, and a restricted cycle theorem

The support translation, abstract question and realizability restriction must be read together. TUZA-10 has no new Lean theorem.

### R (unproved)
For every finite simple triangle-free graph J=(V,E), every proper edge-color map c:E $\to$ C, and every real nonnegative vector x with vertex sums exactly 1 and color sums at most 1, vc(J) $\le$ 2 $\rho$ (J,c). Here vc uses ONLY vertices in V. A rainbow matching has disjoint endpoints and distinct colors. Each x_e $\le$ 1 follows from a vertex equation. Zero edge weights are allowed; isolated vertices are excluded except the empty graph. Summing vertex equations gives sum x=|V|/2. Rational certificates suffice: the feasible polytope has rational coefficients and a nonempty such bounded polytope has a rational vertex.

Do not replace vc by an unrestricted hypergraph transversal or rho by the ordinary matching number. The associated 3-uniform hypergraph has vertex set V $\sqcup$ C and triples {u,v,c(uv)}. It is linear because J is simple and properly colored. Its matching number is rho, but its transversal number may be strictly smaller than vc. It is 3-partite with sides A,B,C if J is bipartite with sides A,B; a general triangle-free graph need not admit such a bipartition. These distinctions persist under saturation.

### Verified translation from TUZA-09
Source: accepted TUZA-09 [LP_GEOMETRY.md](../../problems/TUZA-09/notes/LP_GEOMETRY.md), sections 7–8. Let G be finite simple and y an OPTIMAL fractional edge cover of all graph triangles, with values 0 or 1/2. Put B={e:y_e=1/2}, Z={e:y_e=0}; require the graph (V(G),B) triangle-free. Every triangle has exactly two B edges (feasibility excludes fewer; triangle-freeness excludes three).

Vertices of J are actual B edges. Each G triangle gives an edge joining its two B edges, colored by its Z edge. Two B edges determine at most one triangle, so J is simple. For fixed Z edge ab, triangles abv have pairwise disjoint pairs {av,bv} as v varies, so coloring is proper. A triangle in J would correspond to three pairwise incident B edges. Three pairwise incident distinct simple-graph edges either form a triangle (excluded) or a star. A star would force all three edges among its leaves to be in Z, forming a triangle of y-weight zero (excluded). Therefore J is triangle-free.

### Implication boundaries
Proved translation + R would give tau(G) $\le$ tau_B(G)=vc(J) $\le$ 2rho(J,c)=2nu(G) for the stated optimal-zero/half triangle-free-support class. No reduction from arbitrary G to this class is available. Universal half-integrality is already false; restrictions on the *auxiliary J* in the fallback narrow the class further. The ordinary triangle-free support graph B and its auxiliary J are distinct graphs.

The fallback cycle theorem applies only when J itself is a disjoint union of cycles of length $\ge$ 4 and each color occurs at most twice. In that class x_e=1/2 is an explicit certificate. Even a proof with a better coefficient in that class does not settle R or unrestricted Tuza.

Let J be a finite disjoint union of cycles, each of length at least four, properly edge-colored so that each color occurs at most twice. Let k count its alternating bichromatic C4 components. Then

### The specific unproved sharpening

For the same class, conjecture vc(J) $\le$ 2k+(5/3)(rho(J,c)-k). A single C9 with consecutive colors a,b,a,c,d,c,e,f,e has vc=5 and rho=3: each of the three consecutive triples of edges permits at most one selection, while their middle edges form a rainbow matching. ## 7. Synthesis and prior-art positioning

B1/B2 settle an extension problem with a specific old equality structure. A1 exposes necessary conditions of a hypothetical minimal counterexample but does not classify its tight descendants. TUZA-08 proves a switch and locates a sharp necessary obstruction; W7 shows that cover incompatibility and wedge losses coexist in a non-tight graph. No ancestry-to-neutral-edge argument rules this out in all relevant tight descendants. TUZA-09 shows that scalar fractional or multicover feasibility does not automatically retain the compatibility needed for integral rounding. TUZA-10 rules out an abstract half-integral certificate reduction and explains why genuine graph realizations impose extra closure.

## 8. Verification, provenance and disclosure

The [source-specific ledger](../../STATUS_AND_PROVENANCE.md) maps the selected results to actual declarations, literal types, source proof files and limitations. Mathematical Lean sources and dependency pin files are copied byte for byte. B1/B2, A1 and cover-switch are separate portable projects; no merged build is asserted. Fresh candidate checks rebuild every copied closure module, audit inventoried declarations and replay the resulting objects with the standard Lean kernel. Pinned compiled dependencies are reused. This is neither a cold Mathlib/compiler build nor independent-kernel verification. The only permitted reported axioms are `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`. Finite examples use independent exact integer/rational certificates, with explicit tested domains.

# TUZA-11-15 Research Summary: Sparse Equality, Compatibility and Proof Obstructions

**AI Math Experiments | Technical research report | 3 November 2026**

## 1. The question and the outcome, in plain English

A triangle is a set of three mutually adjacent vertices in a graph. There are two natural ways to measure its triangle structure. We can pack triangles so that no graph edge is used twice, or select graph edges that collectively touch every triangle. Write $\nu(G)$ for the largest packing and $\tau(G)$ for the smallest cover. Triangles in a packing may share vertices. Tuza's conjecture asks whether a cover of size at most twice the packing size always exists [@Tuza1990]. The conjecture remains open in this release.

## 2. Exact statements and boundaries

All graphs in this report are finite, undirected and simple. The triangle family $\mathcal T(G)$ contains **every actual graph triangle**. Covers are subsets of $E(G)$; packings are edge-disjoint members of $\mathcal T(G)$. Let

## 3. Evidence and status across the phase

| Phase | Accepted content | Evidence and remaining boundary |
|---|---|---|
| TUZA-11 | Four-edge flat-piece gluing; five-edge reduction and later gluing; closed-instance kernel; Clebsch obstruction | Ordinary proofs with HKT/Parker inputs; five-edge conclusion additionally uses Liu v1.0.2 with documented erratum. Kernel preserves ordinary optima, not all boundary states. |
| TUZA-12 | Labelled matching root and exact weighted-cover model in the claw-free setting; ordered-lift obstruction; neutral-restoration counterexample | Complete ordinary arguments and exact controls. No general matching root or global bridge. |
| TUZA-13 | Survival in completed tested domains; scoped minimal-failure conditions; exact near misses | Historical finite evidence. Original timeouts and unresolved identities remain UNKNOWN. General S/E open. |
| TUZA-14 | Exact cover-exchange parametrization; unique private-witness and scoped minimal-failure lemmas; shortcut refutations | Ordinary proofs and small exact witnesses. No global augmentation or progress theorem. |
| TUZA-14B | S for $\nu\le4$ or $\tau\le8$; scoped block/slack, attachment, fractional and cut results | Small-parameter S uses Parker/Liu; fractional result uses Füredi. Signed cut remains conditional. |
| TUZA-15 | T0 equality classification; locally bipartite strictness; supporting restoration lemmas | Ordinary proofs plus exhaustive six-link certificates and separate internal AI audit. Prior inequality attributed; no new Lean result. |

## 4. Flat pieces, gluing and an external finite theorem

Call a graph flat when every edge belongs to at most two actual triangles. TUZA-11 considers actual pieces $G_i$ whose union is $G$, whose pairwise edge intersections lie in an actual boundary $B$, and such that **every actual triangle of $G$ belongs to a piece**. Each piece is flat. Noninduced pieces, shared vertices and triangle-free edges are allowed. These are decomposition hypotheses; they are not equivalent to merely adding five edges to an arbitrary flat graph.

## 5. Matching roots, realizability and a neutral restoration failure

TUZA-12 works with the full triangle-conflict graph $X(G)$: its vertices are actual triangles, adjacent when they share a graph edge. Under the actual **claw-free** hypothesis, exceptional $K_5$ and $K_5-e$ triangle components are isolated and handled separately. The remainder has a labelled loopless multigraph root with one root edge per actual triangle. Parallel edges and private leaves are retained. Its underlying simple graph is triangle-free, and its cost-two $K_4$ hubs form an independent set.

## 6. Two-red: exact quantifiers and a smaller difficult domain

Fix a **globally minimum** actual-edge triangle cover $C$. Color its edges red and the other graph edges blue. An eligible triangle has one or two red edges; all-red triangles are excluded. Let $q(G,C)$ be the maximum eligible edge-disjoint packing. Strong S asserts

## 7. Equality through reductions: the proof roadmap

The combined property $P$ consists of Tuza's inequality and the forward equality classification; $B(G)$ implies equality by the elementary clique calculation universally. In a subgraph-closed class choose an edge-minimum failure of $P$, discarding isolates. The earlier local package gives one nonempty triangle component, no triangle-free edges,

## 8. Why arbitrary outside attachments matter

A core reduction deletes some edges, but triangles can extend outside the named core. A valid proof must cover every triangle destroyed by those deletions and must extend a packing without colliding with a maximum packing of the residual. Checking a small core alone answers neither question.

## 9. Exact finite dependency and independent verification

The six-link certificate domain consists of connected six-vertex graphs of minimum degree at least two whose complement has maximum degree at least two. Each nonsymbolic record supplies a matching $M$, a vertex cover $Q$ of $H-M$ within the balanced budget, and either a local packing gain or actual edge-connected residual triangles that cannot have literal clique support. Symbolic records are recognized structurally and discharged by BIP or THREE-SUN.

## 10. Failed mechanisms and remaining questions

Exact failures are part of the mathematical archive. The Clebsch cone has $(\nu,\tau)=(8,11)$ and exactly sixteen minimum covers; private-only packing is five for every one of them. This refutes even an existential private-only half-cover bridge. Two-red eligible packing is eight there. A different unique-witness example has eligible maximum five but maximum four if its specified private witness is forced. Local cover migration can cycle, and eligible/full cover optima can differ. None of these refutes S, E or Tuza.

# A private-triangle obstruction surviving every choice of minimum cover

Recorded 2026-11-01 21:52 UTC. **Ordinary argument with exact finite certificates; not Lean-verified.** Coordinator-generated after seed exposure, independent of the scouts' prompts. Historical priority is unassessed. This is a NO_GO for a specific mechanism, not a counterexample to Tuza.

## Statement

Let H have vertex set F_2^4, identified with integers 0,...,15, and join x,y when x xor y belongs to D={1,2,4,8,15}. Let G be the cone over H with apex a=16. Then

## 1. Clebsch parameters, proved directly

Translation by xor z is an automorphism. Each vertex has the five neighbors x xor D. No two distinct elements of D differ by an element of D: the xor of two unit vectors has weight two, and the xor of the all-ones vector with a unit vector has weight three. Therefore H is triangle-free.

## 2. Classifying every optimum cone cover

Every triangle of G corresponds to a base edge xy of H and is axy. A minimum triangle cover C has a set S of selected spokes. Put U=V(H) minus S. Every edge of H[U] must be selected as a base edge. No other base edge belongs to a minimum C: its triangle is already hit by a selected spoke, and that base edge occurs in no other triangle. Thus every minimum cover has exact cost

## 3. Packing and private family

Triangle packings of a triangle-free cone correspond to ordinary matchings in its base. The displayed perfect matching and the sixteen-spoke bound give nu(G)=8.

## 4. Consequences and evidence

The exact script scripts/clebsch_private_obstruction.py checks all 65,536 subsets U, the full independent-set classification, all sixteen minimum covers, and explicit five-matchings. It uses integer graph combinatorics; no numerical LP or approximation. evidence/CLEBSCH_PRIVATE_OBSTRUCTION.json retains graph edges, covers, packings and the subset counts.

# Independent reconstruction B

Initial independent audit, before access to the two earlier reviewer reports or their evidence. The original target is frozen in FROZEN_TARGETS.md; source references below are to the unchanged author-completed `review/B_AUTHOR_CLOSEOUT.md` (B) and `notes/WEIGHTED_ROOT_LEMMA.md` (W). This reconstruction reads the author's mathematical argument but supplies and checks its missing intermediate details. It is not a blind rediscovery.

## 1. Exact interpretation and triangle components

All triangles are actual 3-cliques. Regard a triangle as its three actual edges when discussing conflict, packing, or covers. Two components of X(G) use disjoint actual-edge supports: an edge occurring in both would make two triangles adjacent. Consequently both nu and tau add over these components, even if their vertex sets meet. Triangle-free background edges do not affect either optimum. Removing a triangle component means removing its support edges, not its vertices. Deletion cannot create triangles, and by component isolation it cannot destroy triangles of another component.

## 2. Residual K4s and triangles outside K4s

After removing the exceptional support components, no triangle belongs to two K4s: if abc belonged to abcd and abce, the preceding exceptional support would already contain it. In particular the sets of four faces of distinct remaining K4s are disjoint.

## 3. Explicit labelled multigraph

For each residual K4 Q choose an opposite edge pair P_Q={e_Q,f_Q} containing every active edge. Such a pair exists by section 2. Introduce a new hub q_Q of weight two. For each actual edge selected anywhere in the construction, introduce exactly one node p_e, globally identified by its actual-edge label e, of weight one. Never merge nodes merely because the corresponding triangles are twins.

### Exact adjacency

Faces of one Q all share its hub, and indeed any two faces share an actual edge. Triangles not belonging to the same Q can intersect as root edges only at an edge-node p_e, and then both contain actual e. Conversely, if triangles not belonging to the same Q share e, that edge is active for any participating K4, so is in P_Q; it is shared for any ordinary participant, so is in P_T. Both represented root edges therefore meet at p_e. This proves a label-preserving isomorphism L(H)=X(residual), not just an abstract line-graph recognition result. It immediately yields nu(residual)=mu(H).

### Triangle-free underlying simple root

A triangle in the underlying simple H could contain at most one hub. If it contained q_Q, its other two vertices would have to be p_e,p_f for the opposite ports of Q, and a root edge between them would represent an ordinary triangle containing both disjoint original edges e,f. No three-vertex triangle can contain four distinct endpoints, so this is impossible.

## 4. Both cover inequalities, including normalization

Let R be any root vertex cover. For p_e in R select actual edge e. For q_Q in R select the two opposite edges of P_Q. If a represented triangle is covered in H at an edge-node, it contains that actual edge. If covered at a hub, one of that hub's opposite edges lies in its Q face. Hence the resulting actual-edge set meets EVERY residual triangle and has cardinality at most w(R); overlap only decreases its size. Thus tau(residual)<=vc_w(H).

## 5. Weighted matching inequality

We independently check W's general claim. Let H be any finite loopless multigraph, S an independent set, and w=1+1_S. Parallel edges do not change matching or vertex-cover optima, so pass to the underlying simple graph without removing vertices (including isolated ones).

## 6. Independent elementary two-edge-neighborhood proof

For an ordinary residual triangle T, choose its two edges containing all shared edges (fill with private edges if needed). They cover T and every triangle adjacent to it in X. For a K4 face T, take the port e in T from P_Q and the opposite port f. They meet every face of Q. Any triangle outside Q adjacent to T shares an active edge in T; by the opposite-port condition that edge must be e. Hence these two actual edges cover the full CLOSED conflict neighborhood of T. This includes missing/dummy ports and triangles attached to multiple pieces.

## 7. Fresh exact checks and scope

`checks/check_b.py` is newly written standard-library code, without reading/importing the discovery or reviewer solvers. It recomputes triangles from all actual edges. Triangle packing uses an independent-set recursion on conflicts; actual covers use a hitting-set recursion; root matching branches on root vertices; weighted root cover branches on endpoints of an uncovered labelled root edge. Witnesses are independently realized/normalized. No prior numerical census count was used as an assertion in the script.

### 1. A self-contained triangle-free high-chromatic base

For a graph B on vertices v_0,...,v_(n-1), its Mycielski graph M(B) has original vertices v_i, clones u_i, and one vertex w. Its edges are all original B-edges, v_i u_j and v_j u_i for every original edge v_i v_j, and all w u_i. There are no clone-clone edges and no w-original edges.

### 2. Twin blow-up and the random-transversal cut inequality

Fix such a base B with b vertices and chi(B)>r. For any positive integer t, let R=B[t] replace each base vertex by an independent set of t labelled twins and each base edge by the complete bipartite graph between the corresponding twin classes.

### 3. The cone has only apex triangles

Let G_t be obtained from R by adding one apex z adjacent to every rim vertex. R is triangle-free: any rim triangle would project to three distinct pairwise adjacent base vertices. For a cone over ANY triangle-free rim R, the preceding correspondence gives nu(G)=matching_number(R). Also tau(G)=vertex_cover_number(R). A vertex cover S of R gives the spoke cover {zv:v in S}. This replacement preserves covering, because uv occurs in exactly one triangle, zuv. The resulting spokes have cardinality at most |C| and their rim endpoints cover R. Take r=4, B=M(M(C5)), and t=24. Then G has 553 vertices, 41,448 edges, and 40,896 actual triangles. Every four-partition has at least 576 monochromatic edges, while 2nu(G)<=552. # Route architectures and final scope

The independent starts are [A_INITIAL](notes/A_INITIAL.md), [B_INITIAL](notes/B_INITIAL.md), [C_INITIAL](notes/C_INITIAL.md). [GATE_1.md](GATE_1.md) records the early decision before consolidation. This file is the final comparison; it does not overwrite the original discovery chronology.

## A — paid nonlocal colour repair

A4 is a single global maximum-four-cut operation after discarding triangle-free edges. Delete all within-part edges F, certify the residual rainbow triangle-edge colouring by F2² differences, and lift an actual cover as F union C_H. No new triangles arise. An actual G-packing P pays if |F|+|C_H|<=2|P|. This would immediately prove Tuza for every graph; the only missing assertion was universal payment, not existence of a maximum cut. All residual covers and global repackings are allowed.

## B — counterexample-preserving compression

Operation: independent twins X have common neighborhood S; let q=|E(G[S])| and require a proper edge colouring of that rim into X. Delete X and all rim edges to obtain R. The q coloured apex triangles use no residual edge; every destroyed actual triangle uses a rim edge. These two certificates prove exact nu(G)=q+nu(R), tau(G)=q+tau(R). Thus delta(R)=delta(G)+q and |V|+|E| strictly falls. Arbitrary outside attachments are included. Prescribed residual triangles/forbidden residual resources are compatible, while exact forced occupied-edge states are not preserved; the diamond distinguishes them.

## C — amplification against the asymptotic theorem

Operation target: put many edge-disjoint copies of fixed G into N vertices with r=Omega(N²), then keep all actual packings below rnu(G)+o(r). Covers cost at least rtau(G). A positive base delta would yield positive normalized deficit, contradicting the uniform asymptotic theorem. The missing step was the integral packing upper bound for every packing, with the full closure family included.

## Remaining bridge and next decision

There is no selected winning route. The clearest unresolved single GLOBAL theorem in the reduction direction would assert that every hypothetical minimal counterexample admits a specifically defined counterexample-preserving move. This run supplies no credible such move set, so that statement is not advertised as easier than Tuza.

# Route C frozen proof and gate assessment

Frozen: 2026-11-03T23:21:57.073173+00:00. This note was independently developed after C_INITIAL.md, before other scouts' arguments were received. Requested Astra/Ultra is not a serving-model attestation.

## Outcome and exact status

**DEPRIORITIZE Route C as a positive amplifier; REDIRECT allocation.** A universal claim that dense copy gluing keeps packing asymptotically additive is false. A precise non-blow-up construction has a finite counterexample to its unconditional packing-transfer component. More generally, the entire class of globally labelled edge-partition gluings has exact cover and fractional-packing transfer, and necessarily loses the original integral gap in the dense limit. This is a proved limitation, not progress toward an unrestricted positive amplifier, and no originality claim is made.

## 1. Published inputs, with exact uniform quantifiers

All graphs here are finite, simple, and undirected, and all triangle families are the complete actual graph-triangle families. Write nu for integral edge-disjoint packing, tau for integral edge covering, and nu*=tau* for the fractional LP optimum.

## 2. Elementary diagnostics

### Disjoint unions

### Disjoint unions

For r disjoint copies, tau(rG)=r tau(G), nu(rG)=r nu(G), and |V(rG)|=r|V(G)|. Consequently delta(rG)/|V(rG)|^2=delta(G)/(r|V(G)|^2)->0. No positive quadratic violation is obtained.

### Equal independent-set blow-up

Let G[t] replace every vertex by t independent clones and every base edge by the complete bipartite graph between its clone sets. Its actual triangles are exactly three clones over a base triangle.

## 3. General fractional-copy obstruction (PROVED_USING_PUBLISHED_INPUT)

**Theorem C1.** Let X have N vertices. Let (H_i,w_i) be finitely many subgraphs of X, each isomorphic to a fixed graph G, with nonnegative real weights such that every edge of X belongs to copies of total weight at most one. Put M=sum_i w_i. Then

**Theorem C1.** Let X have N vertices. Let (H_i,w_i) be finitely many subgraphs of X, each isomorphic to a fixed graph G, with nonnegative real weights such that every edge of X belongs to copies of total weight at most one. Put M=sum_i w_i. Then

    tau(X) >= M tau(G),
    nu*(X) >= M nu*(G),
    nu(X) >= M nu*(G) - e(N) N^2.

## 4. Exact globally labelled gluing (PROVED_USING_PUBLISHED_INPUT)

**Definition.** A labelled edge gluing of r copies of G is a graph X, an edge partition E(X)=disjoint union E(H_i), and a graph homomorphism pi:V(X)->V(G), such that pi restricted to each H_i is an isomorphism H_i->G. Extra isolated vertices of X are harmless. The copies can share vertices in any pattern compatible with pi. No assertion says copies are triangle components.

**Theorem C2.** Every such gluing satisfies exactly

    tau(X)=r tau(G),       nu*(X)=r nu*(G).

## 5. Precise non-blow-up affine construction (PROVED_ORDINARY transfer; Y for limit)

Let G have h vertices. Take a finite field F_q with q>=h and assign distinct field labels lambda_v to the vertices of G. Choose any slope set S⊆F_q. The graph A(G,q,S) has vertices (v,x), v∈V(G), x∈F_q. It has an edge between (u,x),(v,y) exactly when uv∈E(G) and (y-x)/(lambda_v-lambda_u)∈S. There are no edges within a fiber.

## 6. Exact finite witnesses and applicable controls

The standard-library construction and certificate are checks/c_affine_diagnostic.py and evidence/c_affine_diagnostic.json.
