Both were authored in this scout context; independently authored critic verification remains pending.

## 7. Optional refinement: tau(G)<=2nu*(G)-1 when G contains a triangle

**Status: PROVED_ORDINARY using finite LP duality; proof adapts Krivelevich Theorem 8. Originality UNESTABLISHED.** Induct on |E(G)|. Edges in no triangle can be deleted without changing either optimum, so suppose every edge is in a triangle. Choose an optimal fractional cover x and its dual optimal packing.

## 8. Remaining obligation and next-campaign assessment

A successful amplifier must escape these exact interfaces: it must force additional covering requirements beyond the pullback of a base cover, while controlling *every* resulting packing by a genuinely integral argument. Positive quadratic preservation cannot come from merely keeping copied components' packings isolated, using fractional edge-capacity certificates, suppressing o(N^2) closure edges, or choosing a dense partial-slope set.

# TUZA-17 fresh internal AI criticism

Review completed 2026-11-04, within the original mission window 00:45:12–02:45:12 UTC. This is a fresh no-history internal AI review, not a separately commissioned independent final verification. Parent assignment requested Astra / Ultra; serving metadata was not exposed to this critic. No model-serving attestation is inferred.

## 1. Original objections and resolutions

### A-O1: the blow-up colour bound might silently assume monochromatic clone classes

### A-O1: the blow-up colour bound might silently assume monochromatic clone classes

Resolved. For arbitrary clone colour counts, independent uniform representatives give expected base monochromatic-edge count equal to the clone count divided by t². Every representative outcome has at least m_r(B) monochromatic edges. The reverse bound follows by a uniform lift. This establishes exact t²m_r(B) without a uniformity assumption. For B=B0 Cartesian K2, each layer costs at least m_r(B0), and a derangement of all r labels on the second layer simultaneously keeps that cost and avoids monochromatic identity edges. The hypotheses r≥2 and connected triangle-free B0 with chi(B0)>r are adequate.

### A-O2: the prescribed-packing extension might consume a future prescribed edge or unbalance a backbone pair

Resolved after checking the full construction. At a given apex, previous rim perfect matchings contribute forbidden degree at most q−1 and later prescribed edges contribute at most two, hence Δ(F)≤q+1. The current prescribed edges avoid F by induction. Mirrored companions avoid all prescribed endpoints and previous companions, so they cannot introduce a matching conflict. At most six excluded clone positions per class and q+1 forbidden second endpoints are dominated by t≥2q+8. Each prescribed within-layer edge and its companion remove equal numbers from both sides of each affected identity pair; an identity edge does the same directly. With at most two prescribed edges, no pair loses more than two positions on either side. Thus n≥t−2≥2(q+1), and the supplied Hall proof gives a completion avoiding F. Preserving future prescribed EDGES is sufficient: different apex matchings may legitimately share rim vertices.

### A-O3: the strengthened examples might be mistaken for actual critical graphs

Resolved by the explicit negative calculation; this limitation must remain in every summary. Every maximum packing uses all qbt spokes. Removing any spoke lowers nu by exactly one, whereas true criticality preserves nu under deletion of any one or two edges. The explicit cover of size q(b−1)t also gives positive Tuza slack. The examples refute the specified colour repair even after adding fixed codegree/connectivity thresholds, shared-edge triangle connectivity and one/two-triangle extension; they do not refute a claim using the full critical package. The q-apex connectivity proof correctly leaves at least one apex and one rim vertex after fewer than q vertex deletions when bt≥q.

### A-O4: triangle adhesion might discard crossing triangles or use a cover that need not meet the boundary

Resolved at the stated common-triangle scope. The lemma explicitly assumes every actual triangle lies in one piece. Under global packing K+1, gains are at most one. Singleton suppliers in two different pieces would give gain two; hence one piece supplies all three edges and other pieces have zero two-edge gains. The dominant piece's cover meets the boundary because the boundary is an actual triangle. This last step fails for three arbitrary nontriangle boundary edges; the notes correctly retain that gap. The 4-connectivity corollary is therefore a reconstructed known consequence, not a novel global separator theorem. I did not independently audit the entire Freitas thesis or its priority history.

### B-O1: HNS might be used as an unrestricted equality classification

Resolved. The relevant input is for the full 3-partite 3-uniform triangle hypergraph only. Deleting graph EDGES preserves its tripartition. In the 18 March 2018 HNS manuscript I inspected Theorem 1.1 on printed p.3; Definitions 7.1–7.4 on pp.19–20; Proposition 7.5 on p.21; and the Aharoni implication on p.9. I also rendered and inspected pp.19–20. The three auxiliary matchings produce disjoint loose-cycle supports: same-part choices are distinct by matching, and different-part choices are automatically distinct. The graphical conversion to K4 is valid because the two intersecting edges in the third graph triangle must meet. Exhaustion is then elementary: a non-block triangle shares at most one edge with each K4, so one can choose one avoiding face in every block and append that triangle, contradicting the known packing optimum. The argument needs the FULL actual triangle family to include closure faces.

### B-O2: a good arbitrary H-cover might be substituted for a minimum H-cover

Resolved where positive AC is claimed, and retained as an unresolved branch elsewhere. The exact cover identity ranges over ALL H covers. AC requires a cover of cardinality exactly tau(H). The saturation construction has size 2k+m=tau(H) because every inequality in the squeeze is equality. AC-0 has size 2h=tau(H), AC-1e has size 2(h−1)+1=tau(H), and the frontier-essential construction has size m+1+2(k−1)=tau(H). Thus these are genuinely minimum covers.

### B-O3: the packing inequality or deletion type might be reversed

Resolved. Appending M's apex pages to an H−M packing gives |M|+nu(H−M)≤p, hence nu(H−M)≤p−|M|. Coupled with cover loss and Aharoni, this yields tau(H)−m≤tau(J)≤2nu(J)≤2p−2m and m≤b. At m=b every term is equal. At m=b−1, integrality forces nu(J)=p−m and tau(J) in {2k−1,2k}. All these deletions are matching EDGES, with endpoints retained.

### B-O4: outside incidence or block vertex sharing might defeat the chosen packings

Resolved. Blocks are edge-disjoint, not required vertex-disjoint. In AC-1e an e-triangle shares at most one edge with a J block, since two shared edges would force e into that complete block. Choosing avoiding faces gives the required h-packing. A triangle contains at most one induced-link edge because two would place all three vertices in X. This controls its possible intersection with M. In the frontier-essential proof, all surviving old-supported link edges share the unique endpoint of e in X; all other surviving link edges belong to no H triangle and can be appended as apex pages to EVERY maximum old packing. The star-plus-unsupported-edge cover bound is consequently valid. The D=0 branch is explicitly routed to AC-0.

### B-O5: small-budget deductions might use an unjustified triangle-free matching estimate

Resolved, including frozen addendum 1. For every edge of a maximum matching, one endpoint has no neighbor among unmatched vertices: two distinct such neighbors would augment, while one shared neighbor would make a triangle. The single safe endpoint gives vc≤2m−1 for m≥1. Choosing one safe endpoint per matching edge gives m vertices. For m≥3 they cannot all be pairwise adjacent in a triangle-free graph, so two can be removed from the matching endpoint cover, giving vc≤2m−2. This proves the b≤4 corollary with the stated small cases. A remaining counterexample must satisfy b≥5, m≥3, 2m−2>b and m≤b−1. These are necessary conditions only. Two disjoint C5s attain m=4, vc=6 as a link graph, but do not themselves constitute an AC instance or counterexample.

## 2. Later structural supplements

### Critical apex nonsaturation

### Critical apex nonsaturation

Both the original Tutte–Berge argument and the elementary supplement are valid. In the former, a nonempty minimizing set gives a one-vertex blocker; an even component with empty minimizing set gives a one-vertex blocker; an odd edge-containing component gives a two-vertex blocker. The inequalities have the correct directions.

### Tight matching deletion and link-component transfer

Frozen addendum 2 is valid for ANY matching M with tight J=H−M. A J block meeting X belongs to one component because it contains at most two X vertices and any two are adjacent. Each lost old triangle contains exactly one M edge; all its edges meet that component's X vertices. Therefore a lost page can share a block edge only with a block assigned to the same component. Pages from different components share no graph edge, even when their third outside vertex is identical. Distinct J blocks already have disjoint edges, and background blocks avoid X.

## 3. Independent finite reconstruction

New code: `checks/critic_independent.py`. It imports no producer programs or exact_core.py. It rebuilds graphs from literal descriptions, enumerates actual triangles, solves packing by an exact conflict recurrence, enumerates all minimum covers by cardinality, and solves vertex covers and link matchings separately. All arithmetic is integral.

## 4. Input identity and remaining obligations

`evidence/critic_independent.json` preserves SHA-256 identities for the initial frozen proofs, mission and decisive primary/project sources. `evidence/critic_review_inputs.json` records the final reviewed supplements, scripts and evidence, as well as a fresh comparison against the initial hashes. The source content check detects changes; it does not enforce source immutability. New writes were confined to this authorized private workspace with umask 077.

### Proof of items 1–3 and 5–8

A triangle in B cannot cross layers: the only cross-layer edges are the identity matching. Thus triangle-freeness is inherited. # Track B — minimum-cover apex compatibility

**Outcome at this update:** the literal AC statement remains **UNRESOLVED**. No eligible counterexample defeating every minimum residual cover has been produced. The mission has proved several unbounded scoped cases, exact minimum-cover-safe local reductions, and precise restrictions on the first numerical obstruction strata. These are substantive partial results, not a proof for arbitrary graphs or a justification for a longer unrestricted campaign by themselves.

## 1. Frozen literal target and complete state identities

H is finite simple and has a three-colouring of GRAPH EDGES under which every ACTUAL H triangle is rainbow. X is a vertex subset and L=H[X] is induced and triangle-free. G adds a new vertex z adjacent exactly to X. Let h=nu(H), p=nu(G), a=p-h, D=2h-tau(H), b=2p-tau(H)=D+2a, and m=matching(L).

## 2. Proved numerical and structural cases

The full proofs are frozen in [B_FROZEN_v1.md](notes/B_FROZEN_v1.md), [addendum1](notes/B_FROZEN_ADDENDUM_1.md), [addendum2](notes/B_FROZEN_ADDENDUM_2.md), and the independent boundary reconstruction [BOUNDARY_CRITIC.md](notes/BOUNDARY_CRITIC.md).

### Budget four and five are completely settled

In a triangle-free graph of matching number m, a maximum matching has, on each edge, an endpoint with no unmatched neighbor. Removing one such endpoint from its endpoint cover gives vc<=2m-1. For m>=3, two chosen safe endpoints can be chosen nonadjacent, giving vc<=2m-2. In particular m=1,2,3 give vc<=1,3,4. Together with saturation, this proves AC for every b<=4, retaining the distinction that the saturation case supplies SOME minimum cover while the smaller-m cases permit EVERY minimum cover.

## 3. Ordinary minimum-cover-safe ear reductions

The preferred complete proof is [B_FROZEN_ADDENDUM_5.md](notes/B_FROZEN_ADDENDUM_5.md). [Addendum3](notes/B_FROZEN_ADDENDUM_3.md) contains the exact outside-X lambda identity; [addendum4](notes/B_FROZEN_ADDENDUM_4.md) preserves the earlier valid case-split proof. The final deterministic simplification was supplied by the fresh internal critic.

## 4. Failed intermediate mechanisms, kept separate from AC

**Supported-link slack rule:** the stronger assertion that some minimum H cover leaves vertex-cover cost at most D on old-supported link edges is false. H=W5, the cone over C5, has h=2,tau=3,D=1. With X the rim, every L edge is old-supported, but every minimum cover contains at most one rim edge, and lambda=2. The original AC budget includes packing gain and is satisfied. The exact proof is in [A_SLS_RESULT.md](notes/A_SLS_RESULT.md). This does not refute AC.

## 5. Finite work actually performed

All computations reconstruct actual triangles and use exact integer recurrences; no floating-point feasibility verdict is treated as proof. Existing Python3.12.12 only; no solver or package installation. Producer recursion is supplemented by ordinary decisive proofs and, for the core witness, a separate direct subset enumeration of all optimum-cardinality covers.

## 6. Owner-steered boundary realizability work

The boundary argument now proves AC through b=6. At b=6, the remaining link shapes all have a cover-critical edge belonging to some maximum matching. AC failure would force this edge to occur in no minimum H cover, so deleting a maximum link matching containing it forces a tight remainder. The graph-specific packing argument requires at least four edges to belong to EVERY maximum link matching, while the complete link classification permits at most one. This contradiction settles b=6. The eleven-vertex critical-edge lemma has a complete elementary proof in BOUNDARY_A.md and was independently checked by this scout.

## 7. Dependencies, unrestricted relevance, and next decision

Ordinary results include the exact state identities, safe ear transfers, stable-core counterexample, matching-cover elementary estimates and footprint bounds. The tight-remainder results explicitly use Aharoni's tripartite inequality and Haxell–Narins–Szabó's equality theorem through the authenticated TUZA-01 extraction/TUZA-03 exhaustion. Source editions and access limitations are in the central dependency ledger. No unrestricted equality classification, general S/E, or hidden published restoration assumption is used.

# Fresh-context adversarial review of TUZA-18 global gates

Initial review completed 14 November 2026, 17:50 UTC. All work was local on the Mac, except read-only inspection of the public primary reference through the web tool. Mathematical work must stop at 21:00:10 UTC on this date. This is an independent ordinary mathematical review, not Lean verification or external human peer review.

## Context and exact inputs

The reviewer started without the discovery conversation. The initial task supplied only the two frozen proof paths, expected hashes, the campaign stopping rule, and a provenance correction. Before reading other campaign mathematics, I read the canonical `AGENTS.md`, migration handoff, migration report, and these two proofs. The requested reviewer model/effort is `gpt-6-astra / ultra`; I record the request without asserting an independently inspected runtime model identity. The proof titles and status labels were not treated as evidence of correctness.

## Verdict on the two frozen proofs

**No mathematical error found. Both asserted obstruction theorems survive independent reconstruction and the finite attacks below.** Their conclusions have the stated restricted scope. Neither proves unrestricted Tuza, refutes Tuza, establishes historical originality, nor identifies a genuine minimal Tuza counterexample. The publication/download provenance label should be clarified as described below; it is not a mathematical dependency.

## Independent reconstruction: finite incidence restrictions

Fix an integer q >= 1 and 0 < epsilon < 1. It is enough to construct a finite simple 3-uniform hypergraph with arbitrarily small independence fraction, while eliminating all Berge cycles of length at most q. These are compatible requirements because the expected number of bounded cycles is sublinear at the chosen edge density, whereas the absence of a fixed positive-density independent set has exponentially small failure probability.

### Why a Berge forest is a full triangle system

Replace each incidence-tree component by a recursively built graph. A root hypervertex is one graph edge. At a hyperedge reached through its parent hypervertex, the remaining two hypervertices are new because the bipartite incidence graph is a tree. If the parent edge is ab, add a new vertex w and the two new edges aw and bw.

### Random construction, with quantifiers and strict inequalities checked

Set g=max(q,2), a=1/(2g), rho=epsilon/12, and p=N^(-2+a). For each fixed length l in [2,g], an ordered description of a Berge cycle chooses l distinct cyclic hypervertices and a third vertex for each triple. There are at most N^(2l) descriptions. Invalid descriptions may be discarded. For every retained description the l hyperedges are distinct, so its occurrence probability is exactly p^l. Consequently the number X of short cycles satisfies E[X] <= sum N^(a*l) <= g*sqrt(N). Counting the same cycle repeatedly only enlarges this upper bound. Length two is included and removes pairs of triples sharing two vertices.

### Exact no-go implication and its boundary

For a finite forbidden family F of induced 3-uniform hypergraph patterns, take q at least the largest pattern order (and at least one). If a constructed H contained a forbidden induced pattern on U, its full graph realization on U would contradict the premise that the pattern is absent from every full triangle hypergraph. Choosing any epsilon<1 gives tau(H)>2*nu(H), so the proposed enlarged-class inequality is false. The finite-list route would imply Tuza if its inequality were true; the obstruction attacks that sufficient inequality, not Tuza.

## Independent reconstruction: the packing-controlled cut mechanism

The proposed GC statement is: for every finite simple G, some **maximum** triangle packing P and some two-coloring of vertices produce the specified edge set C(P,s) with |C|<=2|P|. A maximum packing is maximal, so every graph triangle intersects B=E(P). This proves the construction is a cover: a monochromatic triangle meets a selected noncrossing B edge; a nonmonochromatic triangle has exactly one noncrossing edge, selected by the appropriate rule according to whether it is in B. These are all possibilities for an actual graph triangle.

### Existence of the rim and linear margin

For N divisible by 20 and p=N^(-2/3), a random graph has expected triangle count binom(N,3)*p^3<N/6. Markov bounds the probability of more than N/4 triangles by 2/3. For k=N/10 the probability of an independent k-set is at most exp(N*log(2)-p*binom(k,2)), tending to zero because the negative term has order N^(4/3). For large N the sum of failure probabilities is less than one. No assumption of independence between the two events is needed.

## Strongest attacks considered

1. **Extra actual triangles in forest realizations:** blocked by the fresh-vertex invariant; full triangle sets were also enumerated independently.
2. **Repeated-edge cycle descriptions invalidating p^l:** the proof expressly restricts to distinct hyperedges, including length-two cycles.
3. **Deleting cycles increasing independence number:** vertex deletion is induced, so the crucial inequality has the correct direction.
4. **Floor effects or missing positive matching:** explicit large-N bounds handle the floor, and alpha(H)<n supplies an edge.
5. **Changing maximum packing to defeat the cone calculation:** every maximum is a perfect matching and covers all spokes; the estimate is uniform in the matching.
6. **Unlisted triangles triggering selected rim edges:** triangle-freeness eliminates rim triangles and the apex enumeration is complete.
7. **Opposite sign in the graph independence lemma:** deletion changes the numerator by d-2>=0, so the induction is valid.

# Private-K4 support for every maximum packing with a common vertex

Status: complete ordinary proof, independently reconstructed by root and fresh critic. This is an all-size scoped PK theorem, not a proof that arbitrary graphs admit such a maximum packing. No originality claim is made.

## Exact statement and global scope

Let G be a finite simple graph and let P be a maximum edge-disjoint triangle packing whose members all contain one vertex v. Write k=|P|, let M be the k pairwise vertex-disjoint edges opposite v, let U=V(M), and let B=E(P). A triangle Q other than a member of P is private for T in P if E(Q) intersects B in exactly one edge of T. A private K4 completion of T is an actual K4 on V(T) together with one more vertex, whose three faces other than T are all private for T. Let A(P) be B together with all edges of all such private completions.

**Theorem.** There is a triangle edge cover C of G with C contained in A(P) and |C|<=2k.

This proves PK-all for EVERY specified maximum packing with a common vertex, in an arbitrary ambient graph. The common vertex need not be universal; vertices outside its neighborhood are allowed, as are unmatched neighbors of v. The cover uses the ORIGINAL A(P), and the proof does not replace P by a more favorable maximum packing. In particular the theorem includes private K4 states and allows cost transfer between packed members.

## Actual triangles and the exact star-maximum condition

Call a triangle old if it avoids v. Every old triangle contains exactly one M edge: otherwise it misses B and can append to P, while a triangle cannot contain two edges of a matching. Let S be the subset of M consisting of edges in at least one old triangle. Write s=|S|, and call these matching pairs active. Every old triangle is therefore an old page on an active base. Its third vertex may lie in U, in N(v) minus U, or outside N(v).

## The two-page exchange and complete pair classification

Take two distinct active pairs i={a,b} and j={c,d}, and old pages Q_i and Q_j on their respective bases. If these pages are edge-disjoint, replace the two packed apex triangles on i and j by Q_i and Q_j. Every other packed member is still disjoint from them, since each old page has exactly one M edge and no edge incident with v. The four apex spokes at a,b,c,d are now free. It follows that every F edge between i and j must belong to Q_i union Q_j: any remaining such edge supplies one more apex triangle and gives k+1 triangles.

## Functional components and an independent halfset

Make a directed graph D on the s active pairs. Each two-edge star gives its directed arc as above. Each mutual root block gives the two opposite directed arcs between its members. Every vertex has outdegree at most one. A star tail has one unique old tip in its head pair and so cannot have another outgoing relation. A member of a mutual block has all its old tips in the opposite member, so it has no other outgoing relation. These facts also prevent overlapping mutual blocks.

## Unmatched neighbors are payable private-K4 sink states

Suppose an active pair {a,b} has a neighbor w in W incident with a. The triangle vaw is private for vab. For any old page abx, if x is not w, the triangles vaw and abx are edge-disjoint and avoid every packed member other than vab. Replacing vab by both contradicts maximum cardinality of P. Therefore every old-page tip on ab equals w. In particular bw is present, the old page is abw, and the four vertices v,a,b,w induce an actual K4.

Status: rejected proposals, not a new theorem or new necessary-condition campaign. Research on this branch stopped before the coordinator's 20:05 UTC generation deadline. No further census was run.

## Distributions over maximum packings

Let P range over maximum triangle packings of cardinality k, and write b(P) for the 0/1 vector of their used graph edges. Genuine edge-minimal Tuza criticality implies that for each edge set S with |S|<=2, some maximum P has b(P)_e=0 for every e in S. Thus the convex hull of the b(P) meets each corresponding coordinate-zero face. This is an exact way to express the already-known one/two-edge packing resilience; it is not a new transfer theorem.

## Private-witness Hall assignment is an old unresolved obligation

A tempting alternative was to associate minimum-cover edges with packed triangles through their actual private witnesses, then seek two units of capacity per packed triangle by Hall's theorem. Private-witness collisions would require mixed two-cover-edge triangles and all-cover-edge triangles to repair the deficient sets. That is precisely the kind of global compatible-packet obligation already recorded in frozen TUZA-14B, Track A sectionsA1-A4: its exact packet budget and cover-repair identity are proved conditionally, but the required global packet or cheaper cover is not supplied.

## Separator or transfer alternative

No new separator operation with an explicit cover/packing transfer and a credible availability argument was found. Inducing a proper subgraph supplies an inductive Tuza bound but does not itself pay for the removed triangles; that missing compatibility is the substantive issue. # Barycentric colourable reduction loses the integral gap, even with arbitrary weights

Status: exact auxiliary reduction gate REFUTED. The construction and weighted obstruction below are ordinary proofs. A standard-library literal checker verifies the fixed K4 instance, every actual triangle and the bipartite incidence certificate. No solver, Lean verification, fresh independent review, historical novelty claim, or Tuza counterexample is asserted.

## The proposed global mechanism

For a finite simple graph G, form its two-dimensional triangle complex: its nonempty faces are the vertices, graph edges, and ALL actual graph triangles. Higher cliques are NOT added as higher-dimensional faces. Let X(G) be the graph whose vertices are these faces, with an edge when one face is properly contained in the other. This is the one-skeleton of the barycentric subdivision of this explicitly truncated complex.

## The complete K4 control

The base K4 has nu=1 and tau=2. Its triangle complex is the boundary of a tetrahedron because the four-vertex clique is intentionally not a face. X(K4) has14 vertices,36 edges and24 actual flag triangles.

## Arbitrary integer edge weights do not repair the control

For a graph Y and nonnegative integer edge capacities w, use the standard weighted parameters: nu_w is the maximum number of triangles counted with integer multiplicity subject to edge loads at most w; tau_w is the minimum sum of w over a triangle-cover edge set.

## Why further subdivision does not remove this obstruction

The same combinatorial argument has an all-size scope. Suppose every original graph edge lies in exactly two actual triangles, and choose a cyclic orientation of each triangle so that the two orientations on each common edge are opposite. In X(G), colour a flag(v,e,T) by whether T directs e away from v or towards v. Flags sharing an edge(v,e) have opposite colours by the assumed old orientations; flags sharing(e,T) use opposite endpoints of e; flags sharing(v,T) use the incoming and outgoing triangle edges at v. Hence the flag dual is bipartite, and the identical incidence proof gives tau_w(X(G))=nu_w(X(G)) for every integer w.

## Archive comparison and stopping boundary

The frozen TUZA18 genuine-cover obstruction required local neighborhood bijections and showed that a triangle-preserving cover of a cone splits into unchanged sheets. X(G) is not such a cover; it creates edge-face and triangle-face vertices and bypasses that rigidity. Its failure is instead numerical, witnessed by a finite integral decomposition. TUZA16's dense-copy obstruction used fractional packing and an asymptotic approximation theorem; none is needed here.

## Sources and verification

The target-class theorem is S. Aparna Lakshmanan, Cs. Bujtas and Zs. Tuza, *Small Edge Sets Meeting all Triangles of a Graph*, Graphs and Combinatorics28(2012),381–392, DOI10.1007/s00373-011-1048-8. Its primary publisher abstract was inspected at https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00373-011-1048-8 ; its full proof was not audited here. Only the hypothetical implication of(B) uses this theorem, not the counterexample or weighted obstruction.

Status: explicit fixed-graph counterexample with independently reconstructed literal certificates and an ordinary construction proof. No exact fractional or half-integral optimum, Tuza counterexample, Lean verification, human verification, or novelty claim is asserted.

## Statement and normalization convention

For a finite simple graph G, define tau_k(G) to be the minimum sum of nonnegative integer edge multiplicities z_e such that every actual triangle T satisfies sum_{e in T} z_e>=k. Multiplicities can be restricted to 0,...,k without changing the optimum. Thus tau_1=tau, and the half-integral cover optimum is tau_half=tau_2/2.

## Literal graph and triangle ownership

Use Petersen rim vertices 0,...,9. Its edges are i--(i+1 mod 5), (5+i)--(5+(i+2 mod 5)), and i--(5+i), for 0<=i<5. Add adjacent apices a=10 and b=11, each joined to all rim vertices, obtaining B=K2 join Petersen.

## Exact half-cover and third-cover

On H, assign weight 1/2 to av and bv for v=0,...,4, and weight zero to ab and the five rim-cycle edges. Every H-triangle has exactly two such spokes, so its load is exactly one. The H mass is five.

## Why the ordinary optimum is 86

The core H has cover number six. If ab is selected, the remaining two-apex rim problem has optimum min_S[2|S|+e(C5-S)]. Choosing the same optimum spoke vertex cover at the two apices proves this formula even when a candidate initially uses different spoke sets. Since C5 is 2-regular, the objective is 5+e(C5[S])>=5, so the total is at least six. If ab is omitted, at least one spoke is required at each rim vertex. A five-cover would consist of exactly one spoke per rim vertex and no rim edge, forcing alternate apex choices around an odd cycle, impossible. The cover consisting of ab and all five rim edges attains six.

## Why the graph has TF and packing resilience

The core H has TF. For an apex triangle abv, use ab,av,bv and the three rim edges not incident with v. For a rim triangle auv, use uv and one spoke at each rim vertex, alternating along the path C5-uv with both endpoints assigned to a; the b version is symmetric. Each is a six-cover containing the specified triangle, and every H-edge belongs to an H-triangle.

## Combining the two certificates at every nonunit order

Let z2 be twice the half-cover, so every triangle has integer load at least two and sum_e z2_e=170. Let z3 be the all-one edge vector, with triangle load exactly three and total 216.

## Exact verification and provenance

The independent checker is `review/halfcover_tf_fresh_checker.py`. It imports no producer code. It reconstructs B,H,D,W from the stated formulas, enumerates all actual triangles, and compares them to the retained literal graph. # Four-branch WKE lemma and unrestricted high-codegree-core localization

Status: ordinary proof with a complete finite certificate domain; fresh independent review pending. The all-size assertion depends on the explicit reductions below plus all5375 finite certificates, not on a census of small graphs. No Lean or human verification, originality claim, or proof of unrestricted Tuza is made.

## Candidate theorem

Every finite simple graph L with at most FOUR vertices of degree at least3 has a WKE witness. There is no bound on its order or maximum degree.

### Isolates, leaves and cycles

An isolate can be removed. If x is a leaf with neighbor v, apply induction to L-{v,x}; add vx to M and v to Q. All newly relevant edges have endpoint v, except vx itself, and |M|,|Q| both increase by1. Removing vertices cannot increase the branch count.

### Two-vertex subdivision lift

If uv is replaced by ua,ab,bv, with a,b fresh, a WKE witness lifts as follows. If uv is in M, replace it by ua,bv and add a to Q. If uv is outside M, an endpoint lies in Q; add ab to M and add b to Q when u is in Q, otherwise add a. Existing Q vertices stay selected, every nonmatching edge is covered, and both sizes increase by1. Iterating lifts any even number of additional internal path vertices. In particular prescribed branch vertices already in Q remain in Q.

### A path returning to the same branch

With minimum degree2 and at least one branch, every maximal path with only degree-two internal vertices has branch endpoints, possibly equal. It has no internal contacts elsewhere. ## Statement and current decision

Let F be a finite simple triangle-free graph with a proper edge coloring, with each color occurring at most twice. A mixed cover is a set of ordinary vertices and colors such that every edge either has a selected endpoint or a selected color. Write tau_mix(F) for its minimum size, and nu_r(F) for maximum rainbow matching size.

## Exact transfer from actual triangles

Suppose the edges of an actual finite simple graph G are partitioned into R and L, every actual triangle has exactly two R edges and one L edge, and each L edge lies in at most two actual triangles. Define F with vertex set R; each actual triangle gives an edge between its two R edges, colored by its L edge. Two graph edges determine at most one triangle, so F is simple. Two triangles with the same L edge cannot share an R edge, so its coloring is proper, and each color occurs at most twice.

## The case nu_r = 1

If the ordinary matching number is one, pairwise intersecting edges in a triangle-free graph form a star and one vertex covers them. Otherwise choose disjoint edges ab and cd. They must have the same color gamma. Every other edge has a different color, since gamma occurs only twice, and must meet both ab and cd to avoid a rainbow pair. It is therefore a cross edge between their endpoint pairs. Two cross edges sharing an endpoint would form a triangle together with ab or cd. Thus the cross edges form a matching of size at most two. If there are two, they must share a second color delta. Selecting gamma and delta covers everything. If there is one, select gamma and one endpoint of that edge. This proves tau_mix <= 2. The empty graph is immediate.

## Necessary structure of a minimal counterexample

Choose an edge-minimal counterexample and discard isolated vertices and unused colors. Put k=nu_r(F). Deleting resources means deleting all incident or corresponding-color edges; the remaining graph stays in the class.

## Complete nu_r = 2 kernel

Every singleton has at least two neighbors in S, whereas S sends at most 4|S| incident edges outward. Thus q1<=2|S|. Every nonsingleton odd component has size at least three; even components only help, so

`checks/fresh_rainbow_resource_gate_search.py` gives each color two edge positions, each selecting exactly one unordered vertex pair. Capacity-one clauses make F simple; incidence variables define endpoints; degree constraints are 2 through 4; triangle clauses forbid ordinary triangles; the two positions of each color are disjoint. For every three positions of distinct colors, an intersection clause requires some pair to share a vertex, excluding rainbow triples. Every set of four mixed resources must miss an edge. A fixed rainbow pair occupies edges 01 and 23 in the first and second color classes. This is harmless because nu_r=2 permits such a pair and vertices/colors can be renamed. For the remaining color classes only, their two edges and then the color classes are lexicographically ordered; these restrictions are also obtainable by edge-position and color permutations and do not disturb the pinned pair.

## The two-resource deletion induction is false

A tempting stronger assertion would say that every nonempty F in this class has two resources whose deletion lowers nu_r. That would immediately give an induction for the desired mixed-cover bound, but it is false even for bipartite 2-regular F.

Let F be a finite simple triangle-free graph with a proper edge coloring c:E(F)→C, every color class having size at most two. # K5-incidence canonical cycle closure: precise gate remains open

Status: bounded structural pass frozen without an all-size closure theorem or counterexample. Two fixed positive controls are retained. No expanded incidence census, generic Eulerian assertion, or H-O2 envelope is claimed.

## Exact proposed statements and why they matter

Let H be a union of literal K5 blocks, distinct blocks meeting in at most one vertex, with every actual H-triangle owned by a block. For U subset V(H), let m(U) be the maximum number of selected rim edges F avoiding U, admitting a proper two-edge-coloring, such that every block's selected edges are contained in some C4 of that block. Equivalently, each block has at least one vertex unused by its selected local edges. This is the resource definition in notes/global_routes_two_apex_k5_states.md; vertices in U remain available to old rim-triangle packings.

## One tempting inference that is not valid

The condition epsilon=0 says m({v})<=m(empty)-1 for every v. It does NOT itself contradict two-spoke resilience: after deleting av and bv, a packing may use abw for a different w. Canonicalization gives the exact profile

## Targeted actual-graph controls

For a connected triangle-free cubic graph B, add two fresh leaf edges at every B-vertex, and take the line graph H of the augmented root. Each original B-vertex now gives a K5 block. Shared rim vertices correspond to original B-edges; private rim vertices correspond to the leaf edges. Two blocks intersect in at most one vertex. Since B is triangle-free and leaves create no triangles, every actual H-triangle lies in one star-clique. The literal checker verifies this ownership directly for the retained controls, without importing a line-graph characterization.

## Why the attempted exchange has not closed

The natural operation is to close an even-length path by routing its endpoints through a third vertex in the K5 containing their missing edge. This adds two edges. Freeing that third vertex costs at most two selected edges, so a naive attachment that tries to protect that vertex cannot force a strict value loss just by degree capacity. However, removing its old incident edges can open an even cycle elsewhere into a new path. The operation transfers the path defect rather than proving that the process ends with an isolated vertex or only cycles.

## Decision and retained unknown

The two decisive structural controls survive, but finite survival supplies no all-size evidence theorem. The strong cycle-only gate and the weaker isolated-vertex gate both remain OPEN. Consequently the K2 join of an arbitrary triangle-local K5 rim has not been proved nonresilient, and no resilient example or H-O2 counterexample has been found.

The sets N_ab,N_ac,N_bc are disjoint. Every independent selection of one apex per label gives an edge-disjoint private three-packing. Let N_i={x}∪A_i, with three nonempty pairwise disjoint exclusive sets. ## Admitted candidate A1 (2026-11-15, initial record before testing)

**Exact statement (CONJECTURE).** Let G be finite and simple, k=nu(G)>0, and suppose every actual triangle T has nu(G-E(T))=k-1 and tau(G-E(T))=2k-2. Then some nonempty component of the actual triangle family, with adjacency defined by sharing a graph edge, has packing number one. Covers and packings are unrestricted graph-edge objects.

**Exact statement (CONJECTURE).** Let G be finite and simple, k=nu(G)>0, and suppose every actual triangle T has nu(G-E(T))=k-1 and tau(G-E(T))=2k-2. Then some nonempty component of the actual triangle family, with adjacency defined by sharing a graph edge, has packing number one. Covers and packings are unrestricted graph-edge objects.

**Unrestricted implication.** Triangle components have disjoint edge supports, and every triangle belongs to one of them, so their packing numbers add. A component with packing number one has a cover of at most two graph edges by the pairwise-intersecting-triangle lemma below. Deleting that cover lowers the total packing number, proving H-D. The known edge-minimal-counterexample implication then proves Tuza. OPEN: all-k component availability, not assumed equality classification.

## Known H-D implication reconstructed

Choose a Tuza violation G with the least number of edges and set k=nu(G). Every proper subgraph satisfies Tuza. For any edge e, tau(G)<=tau(G-e)+1<=2nu(G-e)+1<=2k+1, while tau(G)>2k, hence tau(G)=2k+1. If |S|<=2 and nu(G-S)<=k-1, then tau(G)<=tau(G-S)+|S|<=2(k-1)+2=2k, impossible. For a triangle T, any packing in G-E(T) can be adjoined to T, so nu(G-E(T))<=k-1. Thus 2k+1=tau(G)<=tau(G-E(T))+3<=2nu(G-E(T))+3<=2k+1. Equality gives both H-D premises. This is inherited infrastructure, not new progress.

## Lemma L1: pairwise-intersecting actual triangles

If a graph has packing number one, every two of its triangles share an edge. If all share one edge, that edge covers them. Otherwise choose abc and a triangle abx with x outside abc (if no such triangle exists, abc is the sole triangle). A triangle not containing ab must intersect both abc and abx in edges. The only possibilities are acx or bcx, after relabeling. The six edges on {a,b,c,x} are then present, so all four K4 faces are actual. Any triangle meeting all four faces in edges lies inside this K4: an outside triangle has at most two of its vertices in the K4 and hence at most one K4 edge, which misses two faces. Therefore the entire triangle support is exactly K4. Its two opposite edges cover all four faces. In particular nu=1,tau=2 forces literal K4 triangle support.

## Theorem L2: complete H-D classification at k=2 (ordinary proof candidate)

Suppose the H-D premises hold with k=2. Fix a triangle T. L1 says the full triangle support of G-E(T) is a literal K4 on U. Since no edge of T lies in that K4, |V(T) intersect U|<=1.

## Initial boundary diagnosis

If a residual K4 cell U is edge-component-isolated in H=G-E(T), then |U intersect T|<=1. If U and T are vertex-disjoint, no restored triangle can share a U edge, so U remains a packing-one component in G. Every rim edge induced by W must belong to D, since its triangle has neither spoke selected. Conversely the spokes at S together with all edges of L[W] cover every triangle. ### Exact full and private packing numbers

# Regeneration assessment after the initial routes stalled

Recommendation: **do not promote a surviving reformulation into the main effort**. The campaign has considered a materially different minimum-ordinary-cover architecture, including the refuted private-only proposal C21-C and a full-triangle extension successor C21-D. The remaining proposals below have explicit gaps and no concrete next structural action justified by this scout. This is not a claim that Tuza, H-D or PK is false or that research on them should end permanently.

## Why minimum covers constitute a different architecture

The initial PK program fixes a maximum triangle packing and restricts cover choices to its support/completions. The regenerated program fixes a minimum ordinary cover C and studies private witness triangles with exactly one C-edge. It has neither a permitted-support restriction nor the old compulsory-gain rule. The Clebsch-cone obstruction communicated by the coordinator defeats the private-only universal packing bound: tau is n−alpha, while a private packing uses distinct vertices of a maximum independent set and has at most alpha triangles. This analysis does not depend on the scout's failed lender-only pair reduction.

## C21-D: maximum private packing followed by full extension

The seven-item pretest admission record is `notes/pk_successor_candidate.md`. Its strongest version says: every maximum packing Q of F_C extends, by any inclusion-maximal full extension P, to |C|<=2|P|. The weaker quantifiers “every Q has some successful extension” and “some C,Q has a successful extension” are explicitly separate. A bad greedy extension would not refute the existential versions.

### Bounded test and its exact lack of leverage

`scripts/pk_successor_probe.py` tested 34 named cell/template cases representing31 distinct literal edge sets. It examined341 minimum covers, with a64-cover cap reached on the vertex-sum of two K5s. Unexamined covers in that case remain UNKNOWN in the finite record. All actual triangles were reconstructed; the packing and cover calculations use integer finite recurrences, no numerical solver. No random graph census was run.

## Other materially different representations considered

**All C-edge color patterns.** Retain every triangle classified by whether it contains one, two or three C edges, rather than throwing away the latter two classes. Minimum-cover optimality says that for every X subset C, replacing X requires a cover of all triangles whose C-intersection is contained in X. This is exact and exposes the information lost by F_C, but it is still a complete constraint system. No laminarity, matching duality, exchange axiom or integrality statement was derived from graph endpoints. Claiming that compatible color states exist would merely restate the unrestricted obligation.

## Campaign decision relevance

The regeneration stage therefore did more than rename optional gains: it reversed the packing/cover starting point, tested a precise private-witness assertion, diagnosed its failure through lost color patterns, and screened a full-triangle extension successor. The surviving representations require a new structural lemma before they justify substantial further effort. On the evidence available to this scout, there is no concrete supported next step beyond that missing theorem. An early closeout after independent verification of the actual counterexample is defensible under the mission's stopping rule; it retires current mechanisms and records open alternatives, without declaring a wider impossibility or authorizing a follow-on campaign.

# R2: arbitrary two-edge equality restoration — frozen proof v1

Author role: TUZA-22 restoration agent. Frozen 2026-11-15 UTC for fresh AI reconstruction. Status at freeze: ORDINARY_PROOF_CANDIDATE, pending independent review. This is not a Lean proof or a claim of historical priority.

## Exact statement

Let H be any finite simple graph satisfying B: every nonempty shared-edge-connected component of its **entire actual triangle family** has literal K4 or K5 edge support. Triangle-free background edges and shared vertices of different components are allowed. Let F be a set of at most two distinct nonedges of H, and G=H+F. If tau(G)=2nu(G), then B(G).

## Elementary block facts used

Packing and cover numbers add over actual triangle components. K4 has (nu,tau)=(1,2); K5 has (2,4). Every edge of either clique belongs to some minimum triangle cover, and a maximum packing can avoid any one prescribed edge. These are elementary and are also the pinned public manuscript `papers/tuza-five-degenerate/main.md`, Lemma 2. The stronger known K5 two-edge avoidance is **not needed** for the R2 proof below.

## Lemma 1: the whole one-nonedge page footprint

Fix a nonedge uv of H. Its ordinary pages are the triangles uvx in H+uv, namely x with ux,vx both in E(H). In any one old clique component K, the union of all page spokes ux,vx contains **at most one edge**.

## Lemma 2: preliminary consequences of tight two-edge restoration

If G has no new triangle, B(G)=B(H). If |F|<=1 and G has a new triangle, standard insertion gives nu(G)>=m+1 and tau(G)<=2m+1, so equality is impossible.

## Case A: the new edges meet

Write e=ab and f=ac, with a,b,c distinct. An ordinary e-page is abx where x is outside {a,b,c}, because ac is absent from H; similarly an ordinary f-page is acy with y outside that set. Such two pages share an edge if and only if x=y, their common edge then being ax.

## Case B: the new edges are disjoint

Write e=ab and f=cd, with all four vertices distinct. An ordinary e-page abx and ordinary f-page cdy can share an edge only if x is in {c,d} and y is in {a,b}; their common edge is xy. This follows directly by intersecting their vertex sets; neither new edge can be common to the two triangles.

## Dependency and scope ledger

- Inputs: elementary actual-clique parameters, one-edge packing avoidance, every clique edge in a minimum cover, and additivity over actual triangle components.
- No CS induction, minimal-counterexample hypothesis, sparsity/degree bound, ordinary-block characterization, finite census, bounded graph order, solver verdict, or unproved restoration statement is used.
- The entire-footprint Lemma 1 is the symbolic mechanism that handles arbitrarily many pages and arbitrary outside attachments.
- This proves R2 only. A two-edge blocker for a minimum CS failure is still required for the advertised R2 + H-D-CS-min route to CS. The proof does not imply that blocker or unrestricted Tuza.

# Independent reconstruction of R2 — review v1

Reviewer role: TUZA-22 source-audit / independent verifier agent. This first reconstruction was written before communicating a correctness conclusion to the producer. Source read: `notes/r2_proof_v1.md` (frozen proof v1, exact hash recorded below). No census, root search output, CS induction, or producer discussion was used to establish this conclusion.

## Exact theorem reviewed

H is a finite simple graph. Every nonempty edge-sharing-connected component of its full actual triangle family has edge support exactly that of K4 or K5. F is a set of at most two distinct nonedges of H, and G=H+F. If tau(G)=2nu(G), then the same triangle-component property holds in G. Triangle-free background edges, components sharing vertices, arbitrarily many pages, and arbitrary outside attachments are permitted.

## Independent reconstruction

Write m=nu(H). The clique components have additive packing and covering optima, so tau(H)=2m. Every edge lying in a clique component can be required to belong to a minimum H-cover: require it only in its own component and take independent minimum covers elsewhere. Every prescribed single edge of a component can be avoided by a maximum packing there. Background edges affect neither choice.

## Adversarial checks

- **A new edge initially creates no triangle:** handled. A genuinely tight augmented graph with any new triangle forces a bare ordinary page for each of its two new edges; a triangle using both alone would be covered by one new edge.
- **Two-edge triangles:** possible only in the adjacent case; the bare-page consequence forces the remaining old edge to be absent. They are also already covered in the minimum-cover contradiction used to obtain bare pages.
- **Background edges shared across pages:** expressly allowed; the adjacent conclusion uses a shared background spoke. No background edge is incorrectly treated as a packing resource of H.
- **Large footprint versus one page:** the cover construction uses the proved entire-family footprint lemma. The packing construction only needs one ordinary page. These distinct demands are met separately.
- **Vertex-sharing old components:** every optimization is combined over disjoint edge supports, so vertex sharing is harmless. If a purported crossing old triangle existed, the literal definition would already merge components and invalidate B(H); no such triangle is silently omitted.
- **Attachments through new K4 endpoints:** endpoint intersections alone do not merge triangle components. All new triangles were proved to lie inside the endpoint K4, and its old cross edges were proved to be background in H. This establishes edge-support separation rather than assuming it.
- **Empty/triangle-free H:** m=0 is permitted throughout; the tight augmented nonempty graph is precisely the new isolated-in-triangle-support K4 case. F empty or creating no triangle retains B vacuously or unchanged.
- **Cover versus maximum packing quantifiers:** the proof explicitly chooses appropriate minimum covers and maximum packings. It never requires one universal optimizer to satisfy incompatible simultaneous conditions.
- **No hidden minimality:** proper-subgraph CS, cover-criticality, packing resilience, degree bounds and bounded graph order are unused.

## Scope and global obligation

R2 is an all-size restoration bridge, stronger than a finite interface test. It removes the named restoration obligation from the conditional chain “R2 plus H-D-CS-min implies CS.” It does not prove that a minimum CS failure has a two-edge packing blocker. Nor does it prove R1, H-D-CS-broad/min, original H-D, or unrestricted Tuza. No theorem transfer between their hypotheses is asserted.

# Independent R1 reconstruction and unconditional CS corollary

Reviewer role: TUZA-22 independent verifier. First reconstruction recorded before reporting correctness to the producer. Reviewed `notes/r1_proof_v1.md`; source hash and completion timestamp below. No census or symbolic producer consultation supplied a proof step.

## Elementary avoidance inputs, explicitly reconstructed

For K4, a maximum packing has one triangle; choosing the triangle on the other three vertices avoids every edge of a star centered at the remaining vertex. For K5, maximum packing size is two (the elementary parity proof is given in the R2 review). Up to relabeling there are only two patterns of two distinct forbidden edges. If they are 01 and02, triangles034 and123 avoid them and are edge-disjoint. If they are01 and23, triangles024 and134 avoid them and are edge-disjoint. Thus any at-most-two-edge footprint in a K5 can be avoided. Single edges may be included in a minimum clique cover as established in the R2 review. All facts extend componentwise to B graphs because triangle components have disjoint edge supports.

## Reconstruction of R1

Let independent terminals a,b,c in H be completed to T=abc, and put m=nu(H). The old packing plus T gives nu(G)>=m+1; an old minimum cover plus all three added edges gives tau(G)<=2m+3. If tau(G)=2nu(G), integrality forces nu(G)=m+1 and tau(G)=2m+2.

## Stronger unconditional corollary

**Theorem.** For every B graph H and independent triple a,b,c in H, G=H+{ab,ac,bc} satisfies tau(G)<=2nu(G), with equality if and only if B(G).

**Theorem.** For every B graph H and independent triple a,b,c in H, G=H+{ab,ac,bc} satisfies tau(G)<=2nu(G), with equality if and only if B(G).

Proof. The same base bounds give nu(G)>=m+1 and tau(G)<=2m+3. If nu(G)>=m+2, then tau(G)<=2nu(G)-1, proving strictness. Otherwise nu(G)=m+1. The two-page avoidance argument above still applies, without any cover assumption, so all pages pairwise intersect in edges. The resulting new triangle family either shares one base edge (including the no-page case, for which any edge of T suffices), or is exactly the four faces of a K4 as shown above. In the former case one extra edge covers all new triangles; in the latter two opposite K4 edges do. Hence tau(G)<=2m+2=2nu(G). Equality now implies B(G) by R1, and B(G) implies equality by component additivity. QED.

## Adversarial questions resolved

- The terminal-independent hypothesis is essential to the proof's footprint claim and is exactly present in R1. No theorem for arbitrary three added edges has been inferred.
- A component can include one terminal and arbitrarily many outside vertices, but at most two edges from the two selected pages enter it. All have the same terminal endpoint. This is a proved symbolic footprint bound, not a fixed-core enumeration.
- When pages have two different bases, the fourth K4 face is forced by actual edge closure. It is not omitted or assigned a nonexistent triangle.
- Old supported spokes are handled by a deliberately chosen minimum cover. No claim that every minimum cover contains that spoke is used.
- Outside attachments may touch the new K4 vertices. They cannot merge triangle components through a new triangle because the entire new family has already been classified. They cannot merge through an old spoke because each spoke was proved background under equality.
- m=0 is allowed, and T itself guarantees a nonempty augmented triangle family.
- Neither R1 nor the stronger corollary assumes CS on arbitrary proper subgraphs.

## Consequence for the minimal-CS route

Using the independently reconstructed M0 and residual accounting as declared inputs, a minimum CS failure G with k=nu(G) cannot have a tight triangle residual H=G-E(T), since proper-subgraph CS would imply B(H) and R1 would imply B(G). Thus every triangle residual must satisfy nu(H)=k-1 and tau(H)=2k-3 (with nonnegative values, so k>=2). Adding E(T) to a minimum residual cover yields a minimum G-cover containing all three edges of T. This is a necessary condition, not a contradiction: K5 has that cover containment property. The defect-one residual structure and blocker remain unproved global obligations.

# Matching triangle covers: a scoped equality theorem — frozen v1

Coordinator-developed ordinary proof candidate,15November2026. Pending independent AI review and prior-art comparison. Not an unrestricted proof or claim of novelty.

## Exact theorem

Let G be any finite simple graph having a matching M of actual edges that meets every actual triangle. Then tau(G)<=2nu(G). Equality holds if and only if every nonempty shared-edge triangle component has literal K4 support (triangle-free case vacuous). No bound on order, degree, number of matching edges, or triangle-free background is assumed.

## Proof

Discard from M any edge lying in no triangle. Write r=|M|. Every actual triangle has exactly one M edge, since M is a matching. Partition the entire triangle family into r nonempty books according to that edge, called its base.

## Exact global role and limits

This is an unbounded scoped theorem for graphs admitting a matching triangle transversal. There is no claim that a minimum CS obstruction admits one; such availability would itself be a new global requirement. The theorem uses all actual triangle constraints and does not apply merely because selected/private triangles have matching bases. It does not prove arbitrary B-plus-matching restoration: old supported block edges can obstruct simultaneous page packings.

TUZA-22 restoration role, 2026-11-15 UTC. Status at freeze: ORDINARY_PROOF_CANDIDATE pending fresh independent reconstruction. This file is intentionally a full proof candidate, not an admitted global result or a historical-priority assertion.

## Statement R(2 triangles)

Let H be a finite simple graph satisfying B. Let T and U be actual three-edge triangles whose six edges are distinct nonedges of H. They may share one vertex or have disjoint vertex sets. Put G=H+E(T)+E(U). Then

## 1. Exact one-triangle packing interface

Let T=abc be restored to B(H), where a,b,c are independent in H. Let N_T be the family of triangles newly created by this restoration. It consists of T and ordinary pages abx,acx,bcx with apex x outside {a,b,c} and both old spokes present.

## 2. Unconditional inequality and the only tight branches

The two restored triangles themselves append to every H-packing, so nu(G)>=m+2. Their six edges give tau(G)<=2m+6.

## 3. Lower branch: disjoint vertex sets

If one intermediate is tight, R1 has already proved B(G). Assume both are strict. Their new families are books or K4s by q=1. Because T and U have disjoint vertex sets, a triangle cannot contain edges from both restored triangles: two edges of a triangle share a vertex. Thus the full new family is N_T union N_U.

## 4. Lower branch: one shared vertex

Write T=abc and U=ade, with b,c,d,e distinct. In H all six triangle edges are absent. Let J consist of old cross edges between {b,c} and {d,e}. The five-vertex core K=G[{a,b,c,d,e}] has all six restored edges, plus precisely J.

### The core/page compatibility fact

Every old clique contains at most one vertex of {b,c}, at most one of {d,e}, and cannot contain a together with any of b,c,d,e. Thus it contains at most one edge of J. If a two-triangle core packing avoids the base of an outside page, append that page to it. The entire old footprint in each block consists of at most one J edge and at most one page spoke; if both occur, they share a terminal endpoint. A nonincident choice would force one of the absent pairs ab,ac,ad,ae,bc,de. The footprint is therefore a star of at most two edges. Hence these three triangles append to a maximum H-packing, impossible in the lower branch.

### J empty

There are no mixed triangles. If neither intermediate is tight, the one-extra-edge extension plus a two-edge cover of the other new family gives at most2m+3, as in §3. The case of a tight intermediate is already B by R1.

### J={bd}

There is one mixed triangle abd. If both N_T,N_U are books, use their two bases plus bd, at most three new cover edges. If one family is K4, say abc x, and the other a book, use the two-edge K4 cover {ab,cx} plus the other book's base; ab hits the mixed triangle. Relabel for the symmetric case.

### J={bd,be} (two adjacent cross edges)

## Primary-source authentication and scope

Puleo's Definition4.1 in [arXiv:1308.2211v3, Section4](https://arxiv.org/html/1308.2211v3#S4) defines WKE by a matching M and a vertex cover Q of the graph after deleting M, with |Q|<=|M|. Lemma4.4 supplies the corresponding edge-reduction for a union of link components. I inspected these precise passages. They establish the inequality reduction and do not by themselves provide the strict combined-CS contradiction now being reviewed. The publisher DOI endpoint was unavailable through the web tool; the primary arXivv3 text was accessible.

## Unique-perfect-matching lemma

The induction establishing alpha(X-M)>=r+1 for a nonempty graph with unique perfect matching M of size r is correct. In a disconnected graph, every component has its own unique perfect matching, so the inductive independent-set bounds sum to at least r plus the component count. In the connected case, deleting the Kotzig matching bridge uv produces two sides A,B. Because M uses uv, every other matching edge lies wholly in one side, giving unique perfect matchings on A-u and B-v. Each nonempty side remainder has smaller matching size and satisfies the inductive bound. If a remainder is empty, its bridge endpoint alone supplies the required one vertex. The bridge deletion removes every edge between the sides, so the chosen independent sets combine. Their total is(r_A+1)+(r_B+1)=r+1. Taking complements in the2r vertices gives a vertex cover of X-M of size at most r-1.

## General triangle-free WKE component

For a closed triangle-free component L of a hub link, codegree at least two gives minimum degree at least two in L. A WKE pair M,Q yields r hub triangles using only deleted spokes and matching rims, and a lost-triangle cover X=M union{vq:q in Q}. Closedness is exactly what ensures that every triangle through a deleted spoke corresponds to a rim edge within L; arbitrary other link components and outside rim pages are retained correctly.

## Direct odd-cycle proof

For C_(2r+1), r>=2, the displayed alternating matching M and r-vertex set Q cover all nonmatching cycle edges. The balanced deletion therefore produces B(K) and nu(K)=k-r. Codegree gives an outside page on rim01. The rotated matching M' avoids01 and has r edges. Its hub triangles plus that outside page are edge-disjoint. A residual clique contains at most two cycle vertices, so at most one matching rim and at most one page spoke; if both occur they are incident. The K4 star/K5 two-edge compatibility supplies the required k+1 packing contradiction.

## Remaining global gap

The results exclude precise all-size link classes. They do not prove that every possible minimum CS obstruction contains a triangle-free WKE component, and they say nothing universal about dense triangle-free non-WKE links. Nor does the inequality-only published WKE reduction replace the combined-minimality equality argument. The two evidence labels should remain separate in the main status ledger.

Its only possible conflicting book j is the one whose base contains x. Perfect matching for every selection forces every j-choice to meet it. # Combined CS for graphs admitting a forest triangle-edge cover

Status: ordinary all-size proof candidate, assembled from the independently reconstructed self-contained apex-forest link branches. Fresh review of this assembled hereditary-class argument is required. No historical-priority claim is made.

## Theorem

Let G be any finite simple graph that admits a triangle-edge cover C whose selected-edge graph is a forest. The cover need not be minimum. Then

## 1. The class is hereditary

Let F be the class of graphs admitting such a forest cover. If H is an edge-subgraph of G in F, then C intersect E(H) remains a forest and meets every actual H triangle. Thus H is also in F. Vertex deletion and removal of isolates preserve the same property.

## 2. A leaf of any forest cover gives an apex-forest link

Choose any forest triangle cover C of this minimum failure. It is nonempty because G has a triangle. Let v be a leaf of the selected-edge forest, with unique selected neighbor w; thus vw is its only incident edge in C.

## 3. Both apex-forest branches are impossible

If L-w has a perfect matching, apply `apex_forest_perfect_link_exclusion_v2.md`. If it has no perfect matching, apply `apex_forest_nonperfect_branch_v2.md`. Each branch is an ordinary proof valid in an arbitrary class-minimum CS failure and audits the complete selected footprint in every residual K4/K5 block. Both branches contradict minimality.

## 4. Equality has only K4 components

A K5 cannot have a forest triangle-edge cover. Indeed, the restriction of any such cover to its five vertices is bipartite. One color class contains at least three vertices, whose three clique edges are all absent from the selected cover. They form an uncovered triangle. The same restriction argument excludes a literal K5 subgraph in any graph of F, in particular a K5 triangle component.

## Exact scope and missing global bridge

This is a theorem for graphs admitting at least one acyclic triangle-edge cover, not merely for graphs whose minimum cover happens to be a forest. The class has no imposed order, maximum-degree, or density bound. It does not show that an arbitrary graph, or an arbitrary minimum CS failure, admits such a cover. Indeed K5 has no forest triangle cover. Availability of a useful cover structure outside this class remains a separate global obligation.

# Fresh review: nonperfect apex-forest closed links, v2

Decision: ACCEPT at the stated class-minimal CS scope. This is an ordinary argument using the established class-local M0, edge-codegree and closed-link robustness consequences. The new argument does not require Gallai–Edmonds, Konig or Kotzig as external premises.

## Independent matching reconstruction

I first used a different description valid for every bipartite graph: orient nonmatching edges X to Y and matching edges Y to X; forward reachability from unmatched X and reverse reachability from unmatched Y are disjoint, since an intersection yields an augmenting path. The even reachable sides are precisely the vertices exposed by some maximum matching, by symmetric difference. Their neighbors are the odd reachable sides. The even set D is independent, the fixed matching pairs A to D, and the unreached set C is perfectly matched. A maximum matching with k A-D edges has size at most k+(|A|-k+|C|)/2, forcing k=|A|. Thus all maximum matchings use the asserted structure.

## Leaf witnesses and universal maximum-matching quantifier

A nonperfect tree's alternating exploration reaches at least two original exposable leaves. Odd reached vertices have a forward matched edge; nonleaf even vertices have a forward unmatched edge; acyclicity prevents collisions. If the unmatched root is a leaf, count it as one endpoint and explore the other branch.

## Actual triangle accounting and residual block footprints

Removing all hub spokes into the closed link L and the matching P gives a proper subgraph K. The selected edges P plus the hub spokes at Q cover every removed triangle. In particular, a triangle using a deleted rim edge is covered regardless of where its third vertex lies. A triangle using a deleted hub spoke has its other link vertex in L by closedness. The s hub triangles on P append to any packing of K. The class-local minimality inequalities consequently force a tight B residual, or give an immediate contradiction if |Q|<s.

## Final branch

If C in the forest decomposition were nonempty, its unique forest perfect matching would occur in every maximum forest matching, contradicting edge avoidance. Thus C is empty. Swapping a matched A-D edge into a maximum matching missing its D endpoint proves every A-D edge is allowed and every A vertex has at least two D neighbors.

## Provenance, not a dependency

For historical authentication of superseded v1, the original Gallai1964 paper is openly available at https://real.mtak.hu/189486/ with its published PDF; its introduction Satz(E.1) states the decomposition using Ms, Mu and Mb. A primary research-paper restatement is Busch et al., *Packing of Graphic n-tuples*, author-hosted https://dwest.web.illinois.edu/pubs/degpack.pdf, theorem3.6 on PDF page9. Its notation(A,B,C) equals the present(D,A,C). Those documents were inspected online; they are not needed for v2, and no complete revalidation of the general Gallai–Edmonds proof is claimed.

# Actual-triangle closure in home-base hypergraphs

Frozen candidate v1; 2026-11-16. Status: PROOF_USING_DECLARED_INPUT, pending fresh review. The short transfer below is an ordinary argument. The deep hypergraph inequality and equality theorem are imported, not independently reproved here.

## Exact graph scope

Let G be any finite simple graph admitting a map c:E(G)→{1,2,3} for which every actual triangle has three distinct edge colors. No restriction is placed on triangles crossing a proposed decomposition. Then τ(G)≤2ν(G). Moreover, equality holds precisely when every nontrivial component of the triangle hypergraph is the four triangles on the six actual edges of a literal K4. Thus the proposed CS statement holds for this class, with only K4 blocks. Different K4 blocks may share graph vertices; their edge sets are disjoint and no triangle crosses blocks. Edges in no triangle are harmless background.

## Declared external theorem and definitions

The triangle hypergraph H has vertex set E(G), and one three-element hyperedge for every actual triangle of G. Its matching and vertex-cover numbers are exactly ν(G),τ(G). The color classes make it 3-partite and 3-uniform. Aharoni's theorem gives τ(H)≤2ν(H). Haxell–Narins–Szabó Theorem 1.1 says that equality is equivalent to a home-base partition.

## Ordinary closure lemma

Suppose three distinct graph edges r1,r2,r3 have, for every pair, an actual triangle whose third edge lies outside {r1,r2,r3}. The three edges are pairwise incident. Three distinct pairwise incident edges of a simple graph either form a triangle or have a common endpoint. In the triangle case the unique triangle completion of a pair is the third edge of the set, contrary to the hypothesis. Therefore write them ab,ac,ad with a,b,c,d distinct. Their unique pair completions are bc,bd,cd. These three completion edges themselves form the actual triangle bcd. In particular, the six edges are exactly a literal K4.

## Eliminating R blocks

Take any R={r1,r2,r3} in a home-base partition. Matchability, separately in each of the three parts, supplies a W completion for every pair of R vertices. Apply the closure lemma, viewing H vertices as actual graph edges. Its three completion edges bc,bd,cd all lie in W. Consequently H contains the hyperedge {bc,bd,cd} entirely in W. This violates the edge-home property: the hyperedge is neither contained in an F set nor contains two members of any R set. Hence R is empty. Notice that this argument uses genuine triangle closure, not just linearity of a hypergraph.

## Identifying F blocks

A simple truncated Fano plane has four triples on six vertices, every two meeting in one vertex. Any three of its triples form a loose 3-cycle: their three pairwise-intersection vertices are distinct, and the three remaining vertices are distinct. For an F block, take three of its actual graph triangles. Their pairwise-intersection graph edges are r1,r2,r3, and the remaining edges complete the pairs outside that triple. The closure lemma identifies all six edges of F with a literal K4. The fourth actual face is forced, and F contains precisely its four triangles.

## Consequences and boundaries

Any nonclassified graph in this class satisfies the integer strict bound τ(G)≤2ν(G)−1. Hence a global minimum CS obstruction cannot admit a rainbow three-coloring of its triangle edges.

## 1. Every chosen three-page core has three distinct mutual targets

At every triangle core choose a maximum private packing, of size two or three; at every book core choose one page. The potential mutual-target graph J joins two cores precisely when each has a chosen page whose apex lies in the other core. Give a triangle core weight one or two according as its local packing size is two or three, and give a book weight one. Fix a local three-packing at T. Its pages have distinct bases and distinct apices; write them as abx, acy, bcz after relabeling. By Section1 the apices x,y,z lie in distinct mutual-neighbor cores. Let R consist of T and these three cores, of which s are triangle cores and 3-s are book cores.

Consider the neighbor containing x. Suppose it is a triangle core U=xuv. The only center page that can share an edge with a U-page is abx. A U-page on base uv always avoids abx; a U-page on base xu or xv avoids it exactly when its apex is outside {a,b}.

Suppose the core containing x is instead the book base xx'. Any page xx'd whose apex d is outside {a,b} avoids the center page abx and is compatible with every other triangle in P. Its footprint in a literal K-block has at most one edge: the block cannot contain both x and x', since xx' is absent from K. Choosing maximum block packings avoiding these one-edge footprints would again give k+1 triangles.

## 5. Final augmentation by all three bags

For each of the three center bases there is now a bag: K5 if its neighboring core was a triangle and K4 if it was a book. Take a maximum packing in each bag that avoids its center attachment edge. Such a packing exists: a K4 has a triangle avoiding one prescribed edge, and a K5 has a two-packing avoiding one prescribed edge.

This removes all minimum covers made solely of disjoint K2/K3 components from a global or hereditary-class minimum CS obstruction. It uses literal triangle geometry, an actual balanced four-core reduction, and whole-block footprint avoidance; it is not a deduction solely from the weighted target graph.

## Elementary matching decomposition

For a fixed maximum matching in a forest, even and odd alternating paths reaching the same vertex would, after removing their common final tail, give an augmenting path between distinct unmatched roots. One root cannot have distinct routes in a forest. Thus even/odd/unreached sets are disjoint. Every even-reached vertex's neighbor is odd-reached: its matching edge is a predecessor edge, while each other edge extends the path and cannot return to an earlier vertex without a cycle. Every odd-reached vertex is matched and its mate is even-reached. Unreached vertices are matched internally. These facts prove exactly the decomposition used, without importing a stronger general-graph structure theorem.

## All pointed cases

If w sees an even-reachable u, flip the even path to expose u and add wu. A vertex cover of F minus that matching has size at most the original matching number; adding w pays the new matching edge and enforces the anchor. If w has no such neighbor but Z is nonempty, the strict saving inside Z pays for w in Q while M avoids w. If Z is empty, all w-neighbors lie in the odd-reached set A, which covers the forest and apex edges; M again avoids w. The cases include empty F and isolated vertices and require no minimum degree.

## Full-graph induction and anchor

At a selected forest leaf v with parent w, every link edge ab avoiding w must itself lie in C, because its triangle vab has neither spoke selected. Therefore the FULL link minus w is a forest. Deleting all v-edges and M strictly reduces the number of selected edges, so induction applies to the restricted forest cover.

## Weighted TREE consequence

A triangle cannot meet two cover components because any two of its edges share a vertex. Internal triangles on a tree component's vertex set are covered by that component; assigned external triangles have exactly one selected base and an apex outside that set. The accepted forest external-family minmax therefore applies to pages whose bases are outside D.
